  dbExecute(con, glue("ALTER TABLE ctd_raw ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS {q} DOUBLE"))
q_fill <- qual_fallback[!is.na(qual_fallback)]
dbExecute(con, glue("UPDATE ctd_raw SET {paste0(names(q_fill), ' = COALESCE(TRY_CAST(', names(q_fill), ' AS DOUBLE), TRY_CAST(', q_fill, ' AS DOUBLE))', collapse = ', ')}"))
cat(glue("provider flag columns: {length(qual_fallback)} ({length(q_fill)} filled from their sensor flag where the file predates them)\n"))
meas_cols <- d_meas_ctd$`_source_column` |> na.omit() |> as.character()
meas_cols <- meas_cols[meas_cols != ""]
qual_cols <- d_meas_ctd$`_qual_column` |> na.omit() |> as.character()
qual_cols <- qual_cols[qual_cols != ""]

raw_cols <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'ctd_raw'"
)$column_name

# DIAGNOSTIC: a measurement column in the registry that is absent from ctd_raw is
# a silent no-op in the pivot; a numeric ctd_raw column that is NOT registered
# falls through to cast_cols and can break the ctd_cast PK. Report both.
meas_missing <- setdiff(meas_cols, raw_cols)
cast_leftover <- setdiff(raw_cols, c(meas_cols, qual_cols, "depth_m", "_source_file"))

cat(glue("registered measurement types : {nrow(d_meas_ctd)}\n"))
cat(glue("  canonical (-> ctd_thin)    : {sum(d_meas_ctd$is_canonical, na.rm = TRUE)}\n"))
cat(glue("  quality-flag columns       : {length(qual_cols)}\n"))
cat(glue("registry columns absent from ctd_raw: {length(meas_missing)}",
         if (length(meas_missing)) glue(" -> {paste(meas_missing, collapse = ', ')}") else "", "\n"))
cat(glue("cast-level columns (-> ctd_cast)    : {length(cast_leftover)}\n"))
Code 
# the canonical set is what ctd_thin and the thinned netCDF carry, so show it
# explicitly rather than leaving it implicit in a flag column
d_meas_ctd |>
  select(measurement_type, units, is_canonical, source_column = `_source_column`) |>
  arrange(desc(is_canonical), measurement_type) |>
  datatable(
    rownames  = FALSE,
    caption   = "CTD measurement registry — is_canonical drives ctd_thin membership",
    options   = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE, dom = "ftip"))

19 Split into Tidy Tables

19.1 ctd_cast — cast-level metadata

Code 
# d_meas_ctd, meas_cols, qual_cols come from the Measurement Column Registry above

# use ctd_raw columns (includes ship_key and data_stage added via SQL)
raw_cols <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'ctd_raw'"
)$column_name

cast_cols <- setdiff(
  raw_cols,
  c(meas_cols, qual_cols, "depth_m", "_source_file")
)

# extract one row per cast, keyed (cruise_key, cast_key, cast_dir,
# datetime_start_utc). within that key the only cast-level column that varies is
# lat/lon (sub-meter GPS jitter between same-second scans), so order by it for a
# deterministic pick. measurement-like columns (e.g. ox_aveu_m_sta_corr) must be
# registered in measurement_type.csv so they pivot to ctd_measurement and never
# reach cast_cols — otherwise SELECT DISTINCT would emit multiple rows per cast.
dbExecute(
  con,
  glue(
    "
  CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ctd_cast AS
  SELECT {paste(cast_cols, collapse = ', ')}
  FROM ctd_raw
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY cruise_key, cast_key, cast_dir, datetime_start_utc
    ORDER BY latitude, longitude) = 1
  ORDER BY datetime_start_utc, cruise_key"
  )
)

n_cast <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_cast")$n
say(glue("ctd_cast: {format(n_cast, big.mark = ',')} rows"))

# assign deterministic UUID from composite natural key (md5-based, DuckDB-native)
assign_deterministic_uuids_md5(
  con = con,
  table_name = "ctd_cast",
  id_col = "ctd_cast_uuid",
  key_cols = c("cruise_key", "cast_key", "cast_dir", "datetime_start_utc")
)

# guard: ctd_cast_uuid must be a valid unique PK — fail loudly if a
# measurement-like column ever leaks into cast_cols again (see #53)
stopifnot(
  "ctd_cast_uuid is not unique" =
    dbGetQuery(
      con,
      "SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT ctd_cast_uuid) AS n FROM ctd_cast"
    )$n == 0)

19.2 ctd_measurement — long-format sensor readings

Code 
# add ctd_cast_uuid to ctd_raw for FK linkage
dbExecute(
  con,
  "
  ALTER TABLE ctd_raw ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS ctd_cast_uuid VARCHAR"
)
dbExecute(
  con,
  "
  UPDATE ctd_raw AS r
  SET ctd_cast_uuid = c.ctd_cast_uuid
  FROM ctd_cast AS c
  WHERE r.cruise_key   = c.cruise_key
    AND r.cast_key     = c.cast_key
    AND r.cast_dir     = c.cast_dir
    AND r.datetime_start_utc = c.datetime_start_utc"
)

# --- the two-sensor averages are NOT repaired here -----------------------------
# The source's pre-computed averages (TempAve, SaltAve_Corr, OxAve_StaCorr,
# OxAveuM_StaCorr) are rebuilt from their two sensors by the PROVIDER'S FLAGS in
# § Combine the Sensor Pairs by Their Flags, after the CTD team's accepted flags are
# applied — Rasmus Swalethorp's rule (2026-09-09), calcofi4db::combine_sensor_pair().
# Until 2026-09-11 this spot "repaired" them by the registry's physical bounds alone,
# which let a sensor the source flags 8 (questionable) or 9 (bad) into the average
# whenever its value was physically possible (1,425 temperature and 6,001 salinity
# averages in v2026.09.10) and never saw the accepted flags at all. A physical bound
# is a sentinel guard, not a quality test.

# pivot wide-to-long one measurement type at a time to avoid OOM
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ctd_measurement")

created <- FALSE
for (i in seq_len(nrow(d_meas_ctd))) {
  row <- d_meas_ctd[i, ]
  src_col <- row$`_source_column`
  meas_type <- row$measurement_type
  qual_col <- row$`_qual_column`
  # a series the ingest BUILDS (oxygen_ml_l_ave_cruise_corr, from its sensor pair in
  # [combine_sensor_pairs]) has no source column: nothing to pivot
  if (is.na(src_col) || src_col == "") next

  # a bare NULL is typed INT32 by DuckDB, so if the FIRST measurement type has no
  # qual column the CREATE TABLE below makes measurement_qual an integer column —
  # and the first later type that does have one fails inserting 'nan'. Type it.
  #
  # The source stores these codes in DOUBLE columns, so a plain cast yields "9.0"
  # rather than "9" and no longer matches the controlled vocabulary in
  # metadata/measurement_qual.csv (the CTD set: 0/1/2/8/9). Strip a trailing ".0" TEXTUALLY
  # rather than casting through INTEGER: a numeric cast would silently round an
  # unexpected "9.5" to 9, whereas this leaves anything non-integral verbatim so it
  # shows up in the audit below instead of being quietly normalized away.
  qual_expr <- if (!is.na(qual_col) && qual_col != "") {
    glue("regexp_replace(CAST({qual_col} AS VARCHAR), '\\.0+$', '')")
  } else {
    "CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR)"
  }

  sql_select <- glue(
    "
    SELECT ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m,
      '{meas_type}' AS measurement_type,
      CAST({src_col} AS DOUBLE) AS measurement_value,
      {qual_expr} AS measurement_qual
    FROM ctd_raw
    WHERE {src_col} IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT isnan(CAST({src_col} AS DOUBLE))
      AND isfinite(CAST({src_col} AS DOUBLE))
    "
  )

  if (!created) {
    dbExecute(con, glue("CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ctd_measurement AS {sql_select}"))
    created <- TRUE
  } else {
    dbExecute(con, glue("INSERT INTO ctd_measurement {sql_select}"))
  }
  say(glue("  {i}/{nrow(d_meas_ctd)}: {meas_type}"))
}

n_meas_raw <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_measurement")$n
say(glue("ctd_measurement (pre-sentinel): {format(n_meas_raw, big.mark = ',')} rows"))

# --- strip the -99 missing-value sentinel from MEASUREMENTS -------------------
# -99 is this source's documented missing marker. The notebook already knows that:
# `pseudoNA_values <- c(-9.99e-29, -99)` in the fill_lonlat chunk strips it from
# longitude/latitude. It was never applied to the measurement columns, so -99 has
# been flowing through ctd_measurement -> ctd_thin -> obs as though it were a real
# reading — 84,302 rows in release v2026.07.17, including CANONICAL oxygen
# (oxygen_ml_l_ave_sta_corr 953, oxygen_umol_kg_ave_sta_corr 4,294) alongside
# isus_v 40,479, ph 31,493 and spar 6,189.
#
# The NOT isnan / isfinite guard in the pivot above cannot catch it: -99 is a
# perfectly finite double. A -99 mL/L oxygen silently corrupts any mean, minimum
# or anomaly a consumer computes, which is why this is a DELETE and not merely a
# report — a missing value has no business existing as a row in long format.
#
# Matched exactly (= -99, not a tolerance): every observed case is exactly -99.00,
# and an exact test cannot swallow a real reading that merely rounds near it. The
# two genuinely signed types (dynamic_height, specific_volume_anomaly) are
# reported separately below so a real -99 there would be visible rather than
# assumed away.
SENTINEL <- -99

sentinel_tally <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
  SELECT measurement_type, COUNT(*) AS n,
         COUNT(DISTINCT ctd_cast_uuid) AS n_casts
  FROM ctd_measurement WHERE measurement_value = {SENTINEL}
  GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC"))

n_sentinel <- sum(sentinel_tally$n)
dbExecute(con, glue(
  "DELETE FROM ctd_measurement WHERE measurement_value = {SENTINEL}"))

n_meas <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_measurement")$n
say(glue("-99 sentinel rows removed: {format(n_sentinel, big.mark = ',')} ",
         "across {nrow(sentinel_tally)} measurement type(s)"))
say(glue("ctd_measurement: {format(n_meas, big.mark = ',')} rows"))
stopifnot("sentinel delete accounting" = n_meas_raw - n_sentinel == n_meas)

# --- enforce the registry's declared physical bounds -------------------------
# metadata/measurement_type.csv has carried valid_min/valid_max since the CTD
# registry was built, and NOTHING applied them — not here, not at release time.
# So v2026.08.07 shipped ~31k impossible values: ph down to -10, oxygen_ml_l_1 to
# -79.5, salinity_2 up to 46.3, sigma_theta_1 to -50.8, temperature_ave to -47.6.
#
# The -99 DELETE above only catches the sentinel ITSELF. It cannot catch a
# sentinel that has been scaled, offset or averaged upstream, and it says nothing
# about a genuinely wild reading. A declared bound is the general guard.
#
# This was ~40 lines of inline SQL that ran for this dataset alone. It is now
# calcofi4db::check_measurement_bounds() / drop_out_of_bounds(), which every
# ingest calls and release_database.qmd re-checks — because the same defect was
# live in calcofi_mets.sw_ph (494 values at -99, 16.6% of the type) with its
# bounds declared and equally unread.
# --- declare the PAR sensors' physical bounds ---------------------------------
# `par` and `spar` were two of the nine CTD types with no bound, and v2026.09.06
# published what that leaves in at the release grain: `spar` from -3.07e17 to
# 2.01e16 µE/m²/s (31,623 values on ten cruises, 1995–2008 — 6% of the series) and
# `par` with 34,233 values at exactly 9999 — a fill, not a reading — plus 1,065 more
# above 5,000 and eight below -100 (24 cruises, 1994–2025). Photosynthetically
# available radiation at the sea surface cannot exceed the ~2,500 µE/m²/s the sun
# delivers at the top of the atmosphere, and a dark reading sits within a few units
# of zero, so -100…5,000 catches only the impossible (Ben, 2026-09-10: a certain
# bug, not a question). Idempotent, as the bottle's § Declare and Enforce Physical
# Bounds is.
ctd_bounds <- tibble::tribble(
  ~measurement_type, ~valid_min, ~valid_max,
  "par",                   -100,       5000,
  "spar",                  -100,       5000)
d_meas_type <- calcofi4db::declare_measurement_bounds(
  ctd_bounds, here("metadata/measurement_type.csv"))

# --- the bottle pigments take the bottle database's floors ---------------------
# btl_chlorophyll_a and btl_phaeopigment carried valid_min = 0, which removed 261
# small negative provider values over 2021-07 to 2025-04 (CalCOFI/workflows#131
# item 4): mostly -0.001 to -1.5, a fluorometric reading near zero, which is real,
# not impossible. A bound is a sentinel guard, not the test of "valid". The same
# quantities in calcofi_bottle (chlorophyll_a, phaeopigment) are declared with
# floors of -1 and -5, so these take those floors (decided for #131, 2026-10-04); -99 is still
# removed as the sentinel above and anything below a floor still falls.
# overwrite = TRUE: this deliberately replaces the declared 0.
d_meas_type <- calcofi4db::declare_measurement_bounds(
  tibble::tribble(
    ~measurement_type,   ~valid_min, ~valid_max,
    "btl_chlorophyll_a",         -1,        100,
    "btl_phaeopigment",          -5,        100),
  here("metadata/measurement_type.csv"), overwrite = TRUE)

bounds_pre <- check_measurement_bounds(
  con, "ctd_measurement", mt = d_meas_type)

# report BEFORE deleting: `undeclared` is a finding too, and the seven CTD types
# with no bound are the ones still to take to the provider
bounds_datatable(bounds_pre)

oob_tally <- drop_out_of_bounds(con, "ctd_measurement", mt = d_meas_type)

say(glue("out-of-range rows removed: {format(sum(oob_tally$n_bad), big.mark = ',')} ",
         "across {nrow(oob_tally)} type(s), against ",
         "{sum(bounds_pre$status != 'undeclared')} declared bound(s); ",
         "{sum(bounds_pre$status == 'undeclared')} type(s) still undeclared"))

# the guard must leave nothing behind: a violation here means the delete and the
# check disagree on a bound
bounds_post <- check_measurement_bounds(
  con, "ctd_measurement", mt = d_meas_type, include_undeclared = FALSE)
stopifnot(
  "ctd_measurement must hold no value outside a declared bound" =
    sum(bounds_post$status == "out_of_range") == 0)

# assign deterministic UUID (md5-based, DuckDB-native — single SQL, no R data transfer)
assign_deterministic_uuids_md5(
  con = con,
  table_name = "ctd_measurement",
  id_col = "ctd_measurement_uuid",
  key_cols = c("ctd_cast_uuid", "depth_m", "measurement_type")
)

# add cruise_key for partitioned parquet output
dbExecute(
  con,
  "ALTER TABLE ctd_measurement ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS cruise_key VARCHAR"
)
dbExecute(
  con,
  "UPDATE ctd_measurement AS m
   SET cruise_key = c.cruise_key
   FROM ctd_cast AS c
   WHERE m.ctd_cast_uuid = c.ctd_cast_uuid"
)

# remove orphaned measurements with no parent cast
n_orphan <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ctd_measurement WHERE ctd_cast_uuid IS NULL"
)[[1]]
if (n_orphan > 0) {
  dbExecute(con, "DELETE FROM ctd_measurement WHERE ctd_cast_uuid IS NULL")
  cat(glue("{format(n_orphan, big.mark = ',')} orphaned ctd_measurement ",
           "rows removed (NULL ctd_cast_uuid)"), "\n")
}

20 Apply Accepted QC Flags

The CTD team’s PostgreSQL QA/QC database (server/postgis/init/40_ctd.sql, schema ctd) is a working store beside this release, never a dependency this pipeline connects to live — the bridge is a nightly snapshot, gs://calcofi-db/qc/ctd/flag_accepted.parquet (server/scripts/pg_flag_snapshot.R, cron pg_flag_snapshot.sh), of every ctd.flag row a curator has accepted. This chunk downloads that snapshot, joins each accepted flag to the scan it names, and overwrites ctd_measurement.measurement_qual for the match.

Join key. ctd.file.archive is the zip filename and .path is the member path inside it (libs/pg_ctd.R::pg_ctd_discover_files(): archive = paste0(dir_unzip, ".zip"), path = rel) — byte-identical to this notebook’s own `_source_file` (the d_csv chunk’s path_unzip), so archive reconstructs from it as the text before the first / plus .zip. Within one file, ctd.scan.cast_id / .depth are the verbatim source Cast_ID / Depth columns — flds_redefine.csv renames those to this notebook’s cast_key / depth_m, so (archive, _source_file, cast_key, depth_m) is the same identity as (archive, path, cast_id, depth) in the snapshot. ctd.flag.variable is a ctd.scan column name (e.g. salt1_corr), not a measurement_type — mapped through `_source_column` on d_meas_ctd (built above in “Measurement Column Registry”).

Two flag shapes. A scan-level flag carries depth/cast_id (from the snapshot’s LEFT JOIN ctd.scan); a file/cast-level flag (ctd.flag.scan_id IS NULL, the whole file or cast is being marked) does not, and applies to every scan in that file — for variable = '*' that means every measurement type, not one.

Code 
flag_url   <- "https://storage.googleapis.com/calcofi-db/qc/ctd/flag_accepted.parquet"
flag_cache_dir <- here("data/cache/ctd-cast")
dir_create(flag_cache_dir)
flag_cache_path <- file.path(flag_cache_dir, "flag_accepted.parquet")

# download-first, skip when unchanged: a HEAD request's Content-Length is
# compared to the cached file's size before spending the GET. A size collision
# with genuinely different content is not a concern here — the snapshot is
# COPY'd fresh each night (server/scripts/pg_flag_snapshot.R), never edited in
# place, so "same size" only happens when the file legitimately did not change.
flag_head <- tryCatch(httr::HEAD(flag_url), error = function(e) NULL)
remote_size <- if (!is.null(flag_head) && httr::status_code(flag_head) == 200)
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(httr::headers(flag_head)[["content-length"]])) else NA_real_
remote_last_modified <- if (!is.null(flag_head))
  httr::headers(flag_head)[["last-modified"]] else NA_character_

local_size <- if (file_exists(flag_cache_path)) as.numeric(file_size(flag_cache_path)) else NA_real_

need_download <- is.na(local_size) ||
  (!is.na(remote_size) && local_size != remote_size)

if (need_download) {
  stopifnot("could not reach flag_accepted.parquet and no local cache exists" =
              !is.null(flag_head) && httr::status_code(flag_head) == 200)
  utils::download.file(flag_url, flag_cache_path, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  say(glue("Downloaded flag_accepted.parquet ({round(file_size(flag_cache_path) / 1024, 1)} KB, ",
           "last modified {remote_last_modified %||% 'unknown'})"))
} else {
  say(glue("flag_accepted.parquet unchanged ({round(local_size / 1024, 1)} KB) — using cache"))
}

d_flags <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{flag_cache_path}')"))
n_flags <- nrow(d_flags)

if (n_flags == 0) {

  say(glue("0 accepted flags in snapshot (last modified {remote_last_modified %||% 'unknown'})"))

} else {

  # variable (a ctd.scan column name, e.g. "salt1_corr") -> measurement_type,
  # via the same crosswalk the pivot above used (d_meas_ctd$`_source_column`)
  d_var_xwalk <- d_meas_ctd |>
    select(variable = `_source_column`, measurement_type) |>
    filter(!is.na(variable), variable != "")
  dbWriteTable(con, "_flag_var_xwalk", d_var_xwalk, overwrite = TRUE)
  dbWriteTable(con, "_flags_accepted", d_flags, overwrite = TRUE)

  # the same (archive, _source_file, cast_key, depth_m) identity as ctd.file /
  # ctd.scan (see the section prose above), one row per physical scan
  dbExecute(con, "
    CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE _ctd_raw_keys AS
    SELECT DISTINCT ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m, cast_key, \"_source_file\",
           regexp_extract(\"_source_file\", '^([^/]+)', 1) || '.zip' AS archive
    FROM ctd_raw")
  stopifnot("(archive, _source_file, cast_key, depth_m) is not a unique scan key in ctd_raw" =
    dbGetQuery(con, "
      SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT archive || '|' || \"_source_file\" || '|' || cast_key || '|' || depth_m) AS n
      FROM _ctd_raw_keys")$n == 0)

  # scan-level flags: exact (archive, path, cast_id, depth) match
  dbExecute(con, "
    CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE _flags_scan_matched AS
    SELECT f.flag_id, f.qual_code, f.variable, k.ctd_cast_uuid, k.depth_m
    FROM _flags_accepted f
    JOIN _ctd_raw_keys k
      ON k.archive = f.archive AND k.\"_source_file\" = f.path
     AND k.cast_key = f.cast_id AND k.depth_m = f.depth
    WHERE f.depth IS NOT NULL")

  # file/cast-level flags (no scan_id in the ledger — every scan in the file)
  dbExecute(con, "
    CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE _flags_file_matched AS
    SELECT f.flag_id, f.qual_code, f.variable, k.ctd_cast_uuid, k.depth_m
    FROM _flags_accepted f
    JOIN _ctd_raw_keys k
      ON k.archive = f.archive AND k.\"_source_file\" = f.path
    WHERE f.depth IS NULL")

  n_scan_flags <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT flag_id) AS n FROM _flags_accepted WHERE depth IS NOT NULL")$n
  n_file_flags <- n_flags - n_scan_flags
  n_scan_matched_flags <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT flag_id) AS n FROM _flags_scan_matched")$n
  n_file_matched_flags <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT flag_id) AS n FROM _flags_file_matched")$n
  n_unmatched <- (n_scan_flags - n_scan_matched_flags) + (n_file_flags - n_file_matched_flags)

  stopifnot(
    "accepted flag(s) in the snapshot find no scan in ctd_raw — a broken (archive, path, cast_id, depth) bridge" =
      n_unmatched == 0)

  # apply: named-variable rows go through the crosswalk; '*' applies to every
  # measurement_type recorded for that (ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m)
  dbExecute(con, "
    UPDATE ctd_measurement m
    SET measurement_qual = CAST(x.qual_code AS VARCHAR)
    FROM (
      SELECT fm.ctd_cast_uuid, fm.depth_m, w.measurement_type, fm.qual_code
      FROM (SELECT * FROM _flags_scan_matched UNION ALL SELECT * FROM _flags_file_matched) fm
      JOIN _flag_var_xwalk w ON w.variable = fm.variable
      WHERE fm.variable != '*'
      UNION ALL
      SELECT fm.ctd_cast_uuid, fm.depth_m, m2.measurement_type, fm.qual_code
      FROM (SELECT * FROM _flags_scan_matched UNION ALL SELECT * FROM _flags_file_matched) fm
      JOIN ctd_measurement m2
        ON m2.ctd_cast_uuid = fm.ctd_cast_uuid AND m2.depth_m = fm.depth_m
      WHERE fm.variable = '*'
    ) x
    WHERE m.ctd_cast_uuid = x.ctd_cast_uuid AND m.depth_m = x.depth_m
      AND m.measurement_type = x.measurement_type")

  n_scans_affected <- dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ctd_cast_uuid || '|' || depth_m) AS n
    FROM (SELECT * FROM _flags_scan_matched UNION ALL SELECT * FROM _flags_file_matched)")$n

  say(glue("accepted CTD QC flags applied: {format(n_flags, big.mark = ',')} flag(s) · ",
           "{format(n_scans_affected, big.mark = ',')} scan(s) affected · 0 unmatched"))

  n_flags_applied <- n_flags  # exported into metadata.json below, for release_database.qmd's n_flags_pending
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE _flag_var_xwalk")
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE _flags_accepted")
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE _ctd_raw_keys")
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE _flags_scan_matched")
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE _flags_file_matched")
}
Note

This chunk is shipping unrun this round (2026-09-03): the snapshot is a 600-byte header-only parquet with zero accepted rows (last modified 2026-08-19), so the CTD team has not yet accepted a flag through the ledger. It first has an effect at the next CTD ingest render after the team accepts one. RELEASES.md gets an entry only once n_flags_applied > 0 — a zero-effect chunk shipping is not itself a release-content change.

21 Apply Flag Overrides

The accepted-flag ledger above holds flags a CTD curator has entered against individual scans in the team’s PostgreSQL database. Some flags are known before anyone enters them, most often because the provider’s own cruise notes say a sensor failed. metadata/calcofi/ctd-cast/flag_overrides.csv is where those live: one committed row per (cruise, cast range, direction, series), each with the flag, the reason, the source it rests on and the question that keeps it provisional until the provider flags at source. It is applied after the provider’s flags and the accepted ledger and before any average, so an overridden sensor can never enter temperature_ave or anything built on it: the climatology, the transect shards, measurements.json, the derived dataset.

The file is header-only since 2026-10-20, and the chunk below is the standing machinery for the next entry, not a leftover. Its one entry (2026-09-24, questions.csv Q37) flagged cruise 2026-07-3322 casts 1-6 (both directions): the provider’s cruise notes then said the secondary temperature sensor was faulty on all six, and sensor 2 sat a median 11 °C from sensor 1, up to 42 °C, against 0.002 °C on casts 7-72. It was provisional by design (“until the provider flags at source”), and the provider did: the provider’s corrected file (12 October) carries its own codes, with the secondary temperature, and everything derived from it, flagged 9 where it was bad (casts 1U, 5U, 6D, 6U and part of 5D), and Ben Gire wrote (2026-10-13, 2026-10-14) that the processed files are accurate and that where one sensor is good and one bad the average takes the good one. Ben decided on 2026-10-20 (plan D6) that the provider’s codes in the processed files are the record, so all 24 rows were dropped, including the downcast of cast 1 and casts 2-4, which the provider leaves unflagged although sensor 2 reads about 0.15 °C from sensor 1 there. Those bins now enter the sensor-pair averages on the provider’s word alone. A header-only file is valid: the asserts below hold on zero rows, and a new row (same columns, a reason, a source and a question that keeps it provisional) takes effect again with no code change.

Code 
path_overrides <- file.path(dir_meta, "flag_overrides.csv")
d_overrides <- read_csv(path_overrides, show_col_types = FALSE, na = "",
                        col_types = cols(cast_min = "i", cast_max = "i", qual_code = "c",
                                         .default = "c"))
stopifnot(
  "flag_overrides.csv: every row needs a reason, a source and a question" =
    all(nzchar(d_overrides$reason) & nzchar(d_overrides$source) & nzchar(d_overrides$question)),
  "flag_overrides.csv: cast_dir is D, U or *" = all(d_overrides$cast_dir %in% c("D", "U", "*")),
  "flag_overrides.csv: measurement_type must be a registered CTD type" =
    all(d_overrides$measurement_type %in% d_meas_ctd$measurement_type))

dbWriteTable(con, "_flag_overrides", d_overrides, overwrite = TRUE)
dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE _override_hits AS
  SELECT o.cruise_key, o.cast_min, o.cast_max, o.cast_dir, o.measurement_type, o.qual_code,
         c.cast_key, m.ctd_cast_uuid, m.depth_m
  FROM _flag_overrides o
  JOIN ctd_cast c
    ON c.cruise_key = o.cruise_key
   AND (o.cast_dir = '*' OR c.cast_dir = o.cast_dir)
   AND TRY_CAST(regexp_extract(c.cast_key, '_([0-9]{3})', 1) AS INTEGER)
         BETWEEN o.cast_min AND o.cast_max
  JOIN ctd_measurement m
    ON m.ctd_cast_uuid = c.ctd_cast_uuid AND m.measurement_type = o.measurement_type")
dbExecute(con, "
  UPDATE ctd_measurement m SET measurement_qual = h.qual_code
  FROM _override_hits h
  WHERE m.ctd_cast_uuid = h.ctd_cast_uuid AND m.depth_m = h.depth_m
    AND m.measurement_type = h.measurement_type")

d_override_report <- d_overrides |>
  left_join(dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT cruise_key, cast_min, cast_max, cast_dir, measurement_type,
           COUNT(*) AS n_flagged, COUNT(DISTINCT cast_key) AS n_casts
    FROM _override_hits GROUP BY ALL"),
    by = c("cruise_key", "cast_min", "cast_max", "cast_dir", "measurement_type")) |>
  mutate(across(c(n_flagged, n_casts), \(x) coalesce(as.integer(x), 0L)))
# a series the cruise's file does not carry yet (the corrected forms, before the bottle merge)
# matches nothing, which is fine; an override whose FIRST series matches nothing is a broken
# key, and so is an override row whose cruise has no casts at all in that range
stopifnot("a flag override matches no cast: check cruise_key / cast range / direction" =
  all(d_override_report |> group_by(cruise_key, cast_min, cast_max, cast_dir) |>
        summarize(n = sum(n_flagged), .groups = "drop") |> pull(n) > 0))
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE _flag_overrides")
say(glue("flag overrides applied: {nrow(d_overrides)} rule(s), ",
         "{format(sum(d_override_report$n_flagged), big.mark = ',')} value(s) flagged"))
datatable(d_override_report |> select(cruise_key, cast_min, cast_max, cast_dir, measurement_type,
                                      qual_code, n_casts, n_flagged, reason, question),
          rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 12, scrollX = TRUE),
          caption = "Flag overrides (metadata/calcofi/ctd-cast/flag_overrides.csv) and what each flagged")

22 Inherit Flags Into Sigma-Theta

SigThetaTS1Q / SigThetaTS2Q are blank far more often than the Temp and Salt flags the sigma is computed from: on cruise 2026-07-3322 casts 1U, 5D and 6U the provider flags Temp2Q 9 and leaves SigThetaTS2Q empty, and across v2026.10.19 4,947 sigma_theta_2 bins on 22 cruises were unflagged while their Temp2Q or Salt2Q was 8 or 9 (questions.csv Q45; Ben, 2026-10-20: the provider’s flag outranks everything we derive). calcofi_ctd-derived averages sigma-theta from the two sigma flags alone, so a sigma computed from a bad sensor-2 temperature entered sigma_theta_ave and the mixed-layer depths. Each sigma series therefore takes the 8 or 9 of its own sensor’s temperature or salinity (9 over 8; the provider’s own 8/9 on the sigma is kept) after the provider’s flags, the accepted ledger and the overrides, and before anything is averaged. The rule is inherit_sensor_flags() in libs/ctd_flags.R, tested in tests/testthat/test-ctd_flags.R.

Code 
source(here("libs/ctd_flags.R"))
sigma_inherit <- tibble::tribble(
  ~derived,        ~from,
  "sigma_theta_1", c("temperature_1", "salinity_1"),
  "sigma_theta_2", c("temperature_2", "salinity_2"))
n_sigma_inherited <- purrr::pmap_int(sigma_inherit, \(derived, from)
  inherit_sensor_flags(con, derived, from))
say(glue("sigma-theta flags inherited from the sensor: ",
         "{paste0(sigma_inherit$derived, ' ', format(n_sigma_inherited, big.mark = ','), collapse = ', ')} value(s)"))
stopifnot("a sigma-theta value computed from a sensor flagged 8/9 is not flagged" =
  all(purrr::pmap_int(sigma_inherit, \(derived, from) count_uninherited_flags(con, derived, from)) == 0L))

23 Withhold Series That Do Not Vary With Depth

A value can be physically possible, carry no provider flag and still not be a profile. The provider’s EstNO3_CruiseCorr (type est_nitrate_cruise_corr) holds one value over the whole cast (0-520 m and deeper) on 441 of the 5,066 casts that can be judged, and on every judged cast of seven cruises (2304SH, 2504SH, 2301RL, 2307SR, 2105SH, 2411SR, 0810NH), while EstNO3_StaCorr on the same casts rises from about 1 to 40 µM as nitrate should (census of 2026-10-01; Rasmus Swalethorp’s 2026-09-29 transect-plotter screenshot of line 93.3 showed it as vertical stripes). Most of those values are exactly 0 (an unfilled column), the rest a non-zero per-cast offset: a constant written where a profile belongs. A declared bound cannot see it (the value is in range) and the provider set no flag, so the test is on the shape, and this chunk drops what two tests find:

  1. The whole cast is constant (calcofi4db::check_depth_constant_series()): a (cast, series) with at least 6 finite values over at least 50 m whose range is below 1e-9.
  2. A run of exact zeros within a cast (calcofi4db::check_zero_runs()): at least 6 consecutive values, all exactly 0, over at least 50 m (a step of up to 5 m inside a run; a non-zero value ends it), and only the run is dropped. The station-corrected oxygen ramps to 0 where its per-cast regression fails and stays there (2408SR cast 033: the sensor reads 26 µmol/kg at 322 m, Ox1uM_StaCorr 0.0 from 322 to 517 m); an exact 0 that entered a sensor-pair average would halve it. Bottle-corrected salinity and oxygen only: an exact 0 in the estimated nitrate and chlorophyll is the provider’s estimate clipped at zero where the quantity truly vanishes (nitrate’s zero runs start at the surface beside ~0.1 µM; chlorophyll’s sit below the chlorophyll layer, to the 200 m end of its range, beside ~0.003 µg/L), so those keep their zeros.

The cast is cruise_key + cast_key + cast_dir, one direction of one occupation, never the per-scan ctd_cast_uuid: grouped by that, a “cast” was at most a minute of one and the 2026-10-04 render withheld only 32 cells. On the same data the two tests hold 1,555 constant (cast, series) cells and 710 zero runs (predicted until the next render). Dropped, not flagged: a flagged value still reaches the table and a consumer that forgets cc_qual_ok_sql() would plot it, which is how the stripes reached the screenshot. It runs after the provider’s flags, the accepted-flag ledger and the overrides, and before anything is derived from the series (the sensor-pair averages below, ctd_summary, ctd_thin), so a withheld sensor can never enter an average.

Only the derived and estimated series are judged: a raw sensor that holds still is a different failure. A short cast or run is never judged. libs/census_depth_constant_ctd.R measures how widespread this is across every downcast CSV (data/qc/ctd_depth_constant_census.csv); whether EstNO3_CruiseCorr is a per-cast offset in these files and whether to withhold or recompute it is questions.csv Q42.

Code 
dc_types <- d_meas_ctd$measurement_type |>
  str_subset("^est_|_(cruise|sta)_corr$|^salinity_[12]_corr$")

# --- judge the CAST, not the scan --------------------------------------------
# ctd_cast_uuid hashes (cruise, cast_key, cast_dir, datetime) and the datetime is the
# SCAN's, so in a file with times to the second every depth has its own uuid: grouped
# by it, a "cast" held one value and was never judged. The 2026-10-04 render withheld
# 32 (uuid, series) cells, all in minute-resolution files (2204SH, 2504SH, 1810SR,
# 1501NH), against 441 constant EstNO3_CruiseCorr casts in the census. The cast is
# (cruise_key, cast_key, cast_dir): one direction of one occupation, the grain of
# `sample` (whose key is the cast_key), each direction judged on its own.
dc_cast_cols <- c("cruise_key", "cast_key", "cast_dir")
dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP VIEW _m_by_cast AS
  SELECT c.cruise_key, c.cast_key, c.cast_dir, m.measurement_type, m.measurement_value, m.depth_m
  FROM ctd_measurement m JOIN ctd_cast c USING (ctd_cast_uuid)")
d_const <- calcofi4db::check_depth_constant_series(
  con, tbl = "_m_by_cast", cast_col = dc_cast_cols, types = dc_types)
d_const_judged <- attr(d_const, "judged")

if (nrow(d_const) == 0) {
  cat("no derived series is constant over depth\n")
} else {
  dbWriteTable(con, "_depth_constant",
               d_const |> select(all_of(dc_cast_cols), measurement_type, n, value),
               overwrite = TRUE)
  d_const_by_cruise <- dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT cruise_key, measurement_type,
           COUNT(*) AS n_casts_dropped, SUM(n) AS n_values_dropped,
           MIN(value) AS value_min, MAX(value) AS value_max
    FROM _depth_constant
    GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n_casts_dropped DESC, cruise_key, measurement_type")
  dc_join <- "m.ctd_cast_uuid = c.ctd_cast_uuid AND c.cruise_key = k.cruise_key AND
              c.cast_key = k.cast_key AND c.cast_dir = k.cast_dir AND
              m.measurement_type = k.measurement_type"
  n_dc_rows <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_measurement m, ctd_cast c, _depth_constant k
    WHERE {dc_join}"))$n
  stopifnot("every withheld value is counted once" = n_dc_rows == sum(d_const$n))
  dbExecute(con, glue("
    DELETE FROM ctd_measurement m
    USING ctd_cast c, _depth_constant k
    WHERE {dc_join}"))
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE _depth_constant")
  stopifnot("depth-constant values were not all removed" =
    nrow(calcofi4db::check_depth_constant_series(
      con, tbl = "_m_by_cast", cast_col = dc_cast_cols, types = dc_types)) == 0)

  cat(glue("{nrow(d_const)} (cast, series) pair(s) constant over depth, ",
           "{format(n_dc_rows, big.mark = ',')} value(s) dropped:"), "\n")
  for (ty in sort(unique(d_const$measurement_type)))
    cat(glue("  {ty}: {sum(d_const$measurement_type == ty)} of ",
             "{d_const_judged[[ty]]} judged"), "\n")

  dir_create(here("data/qc"))
  write_csv(d_const_by_cruise, here("data/qc/ctd_depth_constant_dropped.csv"), na = "")
  datatable(d_const_by_cruise, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE),
            caption = paste("Derived series withheld because they hold one value at every depth,",
                            "per cruise and series (data/qc/ctd_depth_constant_dropped.csv)"))
}

# --- a run of exact zeros WITHIN a cast ---------------------------------------
# The whole-cast test misses a series that varies and then holds 0: the station-
# corrected oxygen ramps to 0 where the per-cast regression fails and stays there
# (2408SR cast 033: sensor 26 umol/kg at 322 m, Ox1uM_StaCorr 0.0 from 322 to 517 m;
# 2107SR cast 015u: 0.0 from 55 to 517 m beside 5.6 mL/L), and an exact 0 that enters a
# sensor-pair average halves it. calcofi4db::check_zero_runs() finds each run of exact
# zeros of >= 6 values over >= 50 m (a step of <= 5 m inside a run: bins are 1 m and
# 99.9% of steps in these series are <= 1 m; a non-zero value ends a run), and only the
# run is withheld. Runs left after the whole-cast test, so a cast of zeros only is
# counted there, once.
#
# NOT the estimated nitrate and chlorophyll. There an exact 0 is the provider's estimate
# clipped at zero where the quantity truly vanishes: est_nitrate_sta_corr's long zero
# runs start at the surface (623 of 700) beside values of ~0.1 uM, a depleted mixed
# layer; est_chlorophyll_a_sta_corr's sit below ~110-190 m (1,259 of 1,480 reach the
# bottom of its 0-200 m range) beside ~0.003 ug/L, below the chlorophyll layer. Oxygen
# cannot be 0 where the sensor beside it reads 15-250 umol/kg. (2026-10-04 data; Q42.)
zr_types <- dc_types |> str_subset("^est_", negate = TRUE)
d_zrun <- calcofi4db::check_zero_runs(
  con, tbl = "_m_by_cast", cast_col = dc_cast_cols, types = zr_types)

if (nrow(d_zrun) == 0) {
  cat("no run of exact zeros >= 50 m within a cast\n")
} else {
  dbWriteTable(con, "_zero_runs",
               d_zrun |> select(all_of(dc_cast_cols), measurement_type, run, n,
                                depth_min_m, depth_max_m),
               overwrite = TRUE)
  zr_join <- "m.ctd_cast_uuid = c.ctd_cast_uuid AND c.cruise_key = k.cruise_key AND
              c.cast_key = k.cast_key AND c.cast_dir = k.cast_dir AND
              m.measurement_type = k.measurement_type AND m.measurement_value = 0 AND
              m.depth_m BETWEEN k.depth_min_m AND k.depth_max_m"
  n_zr_rows <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_measurement m, ctd_cast c, _zero_runs k
    WHERE {zr_join}"))$n
  stopifnot("every zero-run value is counted once" = n_zr_rows == sum(d_zrun$n))
  dbExecute(con, glue("
    DELETE FROM ctd_measurement m
    USING ctd_cast c, _zero_runs k
    WHERE {zr_join}"))
  d_zrun_by_cruise <- dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT cruise_key, measurement_type,
           COUNT(DISTINCT cast_key || '|' || cast_dir) AS n_casts, COUNT(*) AS n_runs,
           SUM(n) AS n_values_dropped, MIN(depth_min_m) AS depth_min_m,
           MAX(depth_max_m) AS depth_max_m
    FROM _zero_runs
    GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY n_values_dropped DESC, cruise_key, measurement_type")
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE _zero_runs")
  stopifnot("zero runs were not all removed" =
    nrow(calcofi4db::check_zero_runs(
      con, tbl = "_m_by_cast", cast_col = dc_cast_cols, types = zr_types)) == 0)

  cat(glue("{nrow(d_zrun)} run(s) of exact zeros within a cast, ",
           "{format(n_zr_rows, big.mark = ',')} value(s) dropped:"), "\n")
  for (ty in sort(unique(d_zrun$measurement_type)))
    cat(glue("  {ty}: {sum(d_zrun$measurement_type == ty)} run(s), ",
             "{format(sum(d_zrun$n[d_zrun$measurement_type == ty]), big.mark = ',')} value(s)"), "\n")

  dir_create(here("data/qc"))
  write_csv(d_zrun_by_cruise, here("data/qc/ctd_zero_runs_dropped.csv"), na = "")
  datatable(d_zrun_by_cruise, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE),
            caption = paste("Runs of exact zeros (>= 50 m) withheld within a cast,",
                            "per cruise and series (data/qc/ctd_zero_runs_dropped.csv)"))
}
dbExecute(con, "DROP VIEW IF EXISTS _m_by_cast")

24 Combine the Sensor Pairs by Their Flags

The canonical CTD temperature, salinity and oxygen are the average of a sensor pair, and the source ships that average pre-computed. It is not trustworthy as shipped: where the second sensor is missing, SaltAve_Corr and TempAve are sometimes exactly half of sensor 1 (1998-07-32NM, 2024-01-33UD: salinity ≈ 17 at 1,000 m beside a sensor reading 34), TempAve reads 35–40 °C at 1–2 m on 2003-04-31JD beside a sensor reading 12, and none of these carries a flag. So every average is rebuilt here from its two sensors, by the rule Rasmus Swalethorp set for this project (2026-09-09), implemented and tested as calcofi4db::combine_sensor_pair():

  1. a sensor flagged 8 (questionable) or 9 (bad) is dropped;
  2. a 1 (use primary) or 2 (use secondary) selects that sensor alone;
  3. otherwise the mean of the two, one alone when the other is missing, and nothing when neither survives.

The flags are each sensor’s own (T1Q/T2Q, S1Q/S2Q, Ox1Q/Ox2Q), which the corrected series inherit from their sensor (libs/build_ctd_measurement_registry.R § 4), after the CTD team’s accepted flags (§ above) have been written onto them. A sensor value removed above as a -99 sentinel or outside its physical bound is absent here, which the rule treats like a 9. A physical bound is only that guard: it never decides that a flagged value is good.

Every average is rebuilt, oxygen included, and an average is written wherever a surviving sensor exists even if the source shipped none (Ben, 2026-09-11: Rasmus is the authority on the rule). The source’s own average survives only on a scan where the source shipped no sensor value at all — there is nothing to rebuild it from.

Code 
pair_rule <- tibble::tribble(
  ~ave,                          ~s1,                          ~s2,                          ~raw1,              ~raw2,
  "temperature_ave",             "temperature_1",              "temperature_2",              "temp1",            "temp2",
  "salinity_ave_corr",           "salinity_1_corr",            "salinity_2_corr",            "salt1_corr",       "salt2_corr",
  "oxygen_ml_l_ave_sta_corr",    "oxygen_ml_l_1_sta_corr",     "oxygen_ml_l_2_sta_corr",     "ox1_sta_corr",     "ox2_sta_corr",
  # the source ships no cruise-corrected average; built here (CalCOFI/workflows#106)
  "oxygen_ml_l_ave_cruise_corr", "oxygen_ml_l_1_cruise_corr",  "oxygen_ml_l_2_cruise_corr",  "ox1_cruise_corr",  "ox2_cruise_corr",
  "oxygen_umol_kg_ave_sta_corr", "oxygen_umol_kg_1_sta_corr",  "oxygen_umol_kg_2_sta_corr",  "ox1u_m_sta_corr",  "ox2u_m_sta_corr")

# a sensor series with no flag column would make the rule silently flag-blind
qual_cols <- setNames(d_meas_ctd$`_qual_column`, d_meas_ctd$measurement_type)
stopifnot("every paired sensor series must carry its sensor's flag column" =
            all(!is.na(qual_cols[c(pair_rule$s1, pair_rule$s2)]) &
                  qual_cols[c(pair_rule$s1, pair_rule$s2)] != ""))

combined_sql <- calcofi4db::combine_sensor_pair_sql("p.v1", "p.v2", "p.q1", "p.q2")
q89 <- function(q) glue("regexp_replace(CAST({q} AS VARCHAR), '\\.0+$', '') IN ('8', '9')")
# the same md5 key assign_deterministic_uuids_md5() uses, so a rebuilt row keeps its id
uuid_sql <- "substr(_h, 1, 8) || '-' || substr(_h, 9, 4) || '-' || substr(_h, 13, 4) || '-' ||
             substr(_h, 17, 4) || '-' || substr(_h, 21, 12)"

# the file layout per source file ([rename_fields]); a checkpoint from before
# 2026-09-23 has no such table, which the cross-check reports as 'unknown'
src_format_tbl <- if ("ctd_src_format" %in% dbListTables(con)) "ctd_src_format" else
  "(SELECT CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS _source_file, CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) AS src_format)"

# the provider's own average, beside ours: agreement per layout. The rule is ours
# (Rasmus, 2026-09-09) and it stands; this table is how a disagreement reaches the
# CTD team (Ben Gire, Kelsey Vogel) as a QC finding instead of being a silent choice.
pair_xcheck <- list()

pair_report <- pmap_dfr(pair_rule, function(ave, s1, s2, raw1, raw2) {
  dbExecute(con, glue("
    CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE _pair AS
    WITH m AS (
      SELECT ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m,
        any_value(cruise_key) AS cruise_key,
        max(measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{s1}')  AS v1,
        max(measurement_qual)  FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{s1}')  AS q1,
        max(measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{s2}')  AS v2,
        max(measurement_qual)  FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{s2}')  AS q2,
        max(measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{ave}') AS v_src,
        max(measurement_qual)  FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{ave}') AS q_src
      FROM ctd_measurement
      WHERE measurement_type IN ('{s1}', '{s2}', '{ave}')
      GROUP BY ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m),
    r AS (
      -- did the SOURCE ship any sensor value on this scan (before sentinels and bounds)?
      SELECT x.ctd_cast_uuid, x.depth_m,
        bool_or({raw1} IS NOT NULL OR {raw2} IS NOT NULL) AS src_has_sensor,
        any_value(coalesce(f.src_format, 'unknown'))     AS src_format
      FROM ctd_raw x LEFT JOIN {src_format_tbl} f ON f._source_file = x._source_file
      GROUP BY x.ctd_cast_uuid, x.depth_m)
    SELECT m.*, coalesce(r.src_has_sensor, FALSE) AS src_has_sensor,
           coalesce(r.src_format, 'unknown') AS src_format
    FROM m LEFT JOIN r USING (ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m)"))

  dbExecute(con, glue("
    CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE _pair_new AS
    SELECT p.*,
      CASE WHEN p.src_has_sensor THEN {combined_sql} ELSE p.v_src END AS v_new
    FROM _pair p"))

  r <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
    SELECT
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE v_src IS NOT NULL)                                   AS n_shipped,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE v_new IS NOT NULL)                                   AS n_written,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE v_src IS NOT NULL AND v_new IS NOT NULL
                         AND abs(v_src - v_new) > 1e-4)                           AS n_changed,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE v_src IS NULL AND v_new IS NOT NULL)                 AS n_filled,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE v_src IS NOT NULL AND v_new IS NULL)                 AS n_removed,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ({q89('q1')} AND v1 IS NOT NULL)
                          OR ({q89('q2')} AND v2 IS NOT NULL))                    AS n_flag_excluded,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT src_has_sensor AND v_src IS NOT NULL)            AS n_src_only
    FROM _pair_new"))

  pair_xcheck[[ave]] <<- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
    SELECT '{ave}' AS measure, src_format,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE v_src IS NOT NULL AND v_new IS NOT NULL)             AS n_both,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE v_src IS NOT NULL AND v_new IS NOT NULL
                         AND abs(v_src - v_new) > 1e-4)                           AS n_disagree,
      max(abs(v_src - v_new)) FILTER (WHERE v_src IS NOT NULL AND v_new IS NOT NULL) AS max_abs_diff,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE {q89('q_src')})                                      AS n_provider_flag_89,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE {q89('q_src')} AND v_new IS NOT NULL)                AS n_provider_89_kept_flagged,
      COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE v_src IS NOT NULL AND v_new IS NULL)                 AS n_provider_only
    FROM _pair_new GROUP BY src_format ORDER BY src_format"))

  dbExecute(con, glue("DELETE FROM ctd_measurement WHERE measurement_type = '{ave}'"))
  dbExecute(con, glue("
    INSERT INTO ctd_measurement BY NAME
    SELECT {uuid_sql} AS ctd_measurement_uuid,
           ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m, '{ave}' AS measurement_type,
           v_new AS measurement_value,
           -- the provider's verdict on ITS average (SaltAve_CorrQ, OxAve_StaCorrQ, …)
           -- rides on ours: a value it flags 8/9 stays flagged for every consumer
           -- that applies qual_ok, even though the pair rule rebuilt it
           q_src AS measurement_qual, cruise_key
    FROM (
      SELECT *, md5(concat_ws('|', COALESCE(CAST(ctd_cast_uuid AS VARCHAR), ''),
                                   COALESCE(CAST(depth_m AS VARCHAR), ''),
                                   '{ave}')) AS _h
      FROM _pair_new WHERE v_new IS NOT NULL)"))

  mutate(r, measure = ave, .before = 1)
})
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _pair")
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _pair_new")

say(glue("sensor pairs combined by their flags: ",
         "{format(sum(pair_report$n_written), big.mark = ',')} averages written, ",
         "{format(sum(pair_report$n_changed), big.mark = ',')} changed from the source's, ",
         "{format(sum(pair_report$n_filled), big.mark = ',')} filled where it shipped none, ",
         "{format(sum(pair_report$n_flag_excluded), big.mark = ',')} with a flagged sensor left out"))
datatable(pair_report, caption = "Averages rebuilt from their sensor pairs by the flag rule",
          rownames = FALSE)
pair_xcheck <- bind_rows(pair_xcheck)
write_csv(pair_xcheck, glue("{dir_tmp}/ctd_pair_xcheck.csv"), na = "")
datatable(pair_xcheck, rownames = FALSE, caption = paste(
  "Cross-check: our flag-rule average against the provider's own (SaltAve_Corr +",
  "SaltAve_CorrQ, OxAve_StaCorr + OxAve_StaCorrQ, …) per file layout. n_disagree > 0 is",
  "a QC finding for the CTD team, never a silent choice; ours is what is written."))

# the rebuilt averages must still sit inside their own bounds, and each scan has one
bounds_pairs <- check_measurement_bounds(
  con, "ctd_measurement", mt = d_meas_type, include_undeclared = FALSE)
stopifnot(
  "a rebuilt average fell outside its declared bound" =
    sum(bounds_pairs$status == "out_of_range" &
          bounds_pairs$measurement_type %in% pair_rule$ave) == 0,
  "one rebuilt average per scan" =
    dbGetQuery(con, glue("
      SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT ctd_cast_uuid || '|' || depth_m || '|' || measurement_type) AS n
      FROM ctd_measurement WHERE measurement_type IN ({paste0(\"'\", pair_rule$ave, \"'\", collapse = ', ')})"))$n == 0)

# and the rule itself, asserted on what was written: where a sensor is flagged 8/9 the
# average is the OTHER sensor (or absent) — never a mean that includes the flagged one
n_flag_leak <- sum(pmap_int(pair_rule, function(ave, s1, s2, raw1, raw2) {
  dbGetQuery(con, glue("
    WITH p AS (
      SELECT ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m,
        max(measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{s1}')  AS v1,
        max(measurement_qual)  FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{s1}')  AS q1,
        max(measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{s2}')  AS v2,
        max(measurement_qual)  FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{s2}')  AS q2,
        max(measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = '{ave}') AS va
      FROM ctd_measurement WHERE measurement_type IN ('{s1}', '{s2}', '{ave}')
      GROUP BY ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m)
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM p
    WHERE va IS NOT NULL AND (
      ({q89('q1')} AND v1 IS NOT NULL AND (v2 IS NULL OR {q89('q2')} OR abs(va - v2) > 1e-9)) OR
      ({q89('q2')} AND v2 IS NOT NULL AND (v1 IS NULL OR {q89('q1')} OR abs(va - v1) > 1e-9)))"))$n
}))
stopifnot("an average includes a sensor its provider flags 8/9" = n_flag_leak == 0)

# and the overrides in particular: on every overridden cast the average is the OTHER sensor
# exactly — for Q37, temperature_ave on 2026-07-3322 casts 1-6 equals temperature_1
n_override_leak <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
  WITH t AS (
    SELECT h.ctd_cast_uuid, h.depth_m
    FROM _override_hits h WHERE h.measurement_type = 'temperature_2'),
  p AS (
    SELECT m.ctd_cast_uuid, m.depth_m,
      max(measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_1')   AS v1,
      max(measurement_qual)  FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_1')   AS q1,
      max(measurement_value) FILTER (WHERE measurement_type = 'temperature_ave') AS va
    FROM ctd_measurement m JOIN t USING (ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m)
    WHERE measurement_type IN ('temperature_1', 'temperature_ave')
    GROUP BY 1, 2)
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE va IS NOT NULL AND (v1 IS NULL OR {q89('q1')} OR abs(va - v1) > 1e-12)) AS n_leak,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE va IS NOT NULL) AS n_ave,
    max(abs(va - v1)) AS max_abs_diff
  FROM p"))
say(glue("override check: {n_override_leak$n_ave} temperature_ave values on overridden casts, ",
         "max |temperature_ave - temperature_1| = {n_override_leak$max_abs_diff}"))
stopifnot("an average on an overridden cast includes the overridden sensor" =
            n_override_leak$n_leak == 0)
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _override_hits")

24.1 ctd_summary — summary stats across cast directions

Code 
# one measurement type at a time: every group is (cruise, site, depth, TYPE), so the
# per-type slices are disjoint and their union is exactly the one-statement result. The
# single GROUP BY over ~280M rows needed a hash table larger than the DuckDB budget
# (6 GB, 2026-09-24: "Out of Memory Error ... 5.5 GiB/5.5 GiB used"); it had only ever
# passed because the post-checkpoint connection ran unlimited.
summ_sql <- function(type) glue("
  SELECT
    c.cruise_key,
    c.site_key,
    m.depth_m,
    m.measurement_type,
    AVG(m.measurement_value)    AS avg,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(*) = 1 THEN 0
      ELSE COALESCE(STDDEV_SAMP(m.measurement_value), 0)
    END                          AS stddev,
    COUNT(*)                     AS n_obs
  FROM ctd_measurement m
  INNER JOIN ctd_cast c ON m.ctd_cast_uuid = c.ctd_cast_uuid
  WHERE m.measurement_type = '{type}'
    AND NOT isnan(m.measurement_value)
    AND isfinite(m.measurement_value)
  GROUP BY c.cruise_key, c.site_key, m.depth_m, m.measurement_type")
summ_types <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DISTINCT measurement_type FROM ctd_measurement ORDER BY 1")$measurement_type
dbExecute(con, glue("CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ctd_summary AS {summ_sql(summ_types[1])}"))
for (type in summ_types[-1])
  dbExecute(con, glue("INSERT INTO ctd_summary {summ_sql(type)}"))

n_summ <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_summary")$n
say(glue("ctd_summary: {format(n_summ, big.mark = ',')} rows"))

assign_deterministic_uuids_md5(
  con = con,
  table_name = "ctd_summary",
  id_col = "ctd_summary_uuid",
  key_cols = c("cruise_key", "site_key", "depth_m", "measurement_type")
)

24.2 measurement_type — reference table

Code 
dbWriteTable(con, "measurement_type", d_meas_type, overwrite = TRUE)
say(glue("measurement_type: {nrow(d_meas_type)} rows"))

# validate: all measurement_types used by this dataset are registered
ctd_types_used <- dbGetQuery(
  con,
  "SELECT DISTINCT measurement_type FROM ctd_measurement"
)$measurement_type

registered <- d_meas_type |>
  filter(str_detect(`_source_datasets`, "calcofi_ctd-cast")) |>
  pull(measurement_type)

unregistered <- setdiff(ctd_types_used, registered)
stopifnot(
  "all measurement_types used by calcofi_ctd-cast must be registered in _source_datasets" = length(
    unregistered
  ) ==
    0
)

24.3 Measurement provenance — instrument and accuracy eras

Which instrument produced a value, to what stated accuracy, and over which years. Recovered from the CalCOFI hydrographic master’s 0-Measurements table into metadata/calcofi/hydro-master/measurement_method.csv; the pipeline had no equivalent. It matters most where a method changed mid-record — water temperature switches from reversing thermometer (through 1993-04-15) to CTD thermistor (from 1993-08-11), which is the boundary this dataset begins at, and phosphate crosses four instruments from 1949.

The registry is one-to-many by design (Temperature has 6 eras), so it is joined by property rather than by exact type: CTD types carry sensor and correction suffixes (temperature_1, salinity_ave_corr, oxygen_ml_l_ave_sta_corr) that the era table knows nothing about, so those are stripped back to the base property before matching.

Code 
path_method <- here("metadata/calcofi/hydro-master/measurement_method.csv")

d_method <- read_csv(path_method, show_col_types = F) |>
  filter(!is.na(measurement_type)) |>
  select(property = measurement_type, method, accuracy, year_started, year_ended)

# strip sensor/correction suffixes and the bottle marker to reach the base property:
#   temperature_ave  -> temperature ; oxygen_ml_l_ave_sta_corr -> oxygen_ml_l
#   btl_temperature  -> temperature ; salinity_btl            -> salinity
#   oxygen_btl_ml_l  -> oxygen_ml_l  (the marker is INFIX here, not a prefix/suffix —
#                                     the three positions are why this is not one regex)
base_property <- function(x) {
  x |>
    str_remove("^btl_") |>
    str_remove("_btl$") |>
    str_replace("_btl_", "_") |>
    str_remove("_(cruise|sta)_corr$") |>
    str_remove("_corr$") |>
    str_remove("_ave$") |>
    str_remove("_[12]$")
}

d_prov <- d_meas_ctd |>
  transmute(measurement_type, units, is_canonical,
            property = base_property(measurement_type)) |>
  inner_join(d_method, by = "property", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  arrange(desc(is_canonical), measurement_type, year_started)

n_typ <- n_distinct(d_prov$measurement_type)
say(glue("CTD types with instrument provenance: {n_typ} of {nrow(d_meas_ctd)} ",
         "({n_distinct(d_prov$property)} distinct properties, ",
         "{nrow(d_prov)} type x era rows)"))
say(glue("  unmatched (no era recorded): ",
         "{paste(setdiff(d_meas_ctd$measurement_type, d_prov$measurement_type) |> head(8), collapse = ', ')}",
         if (nrow(d_meas_ctd) - n_typ > 8) " ..." else ""))
Code 
d_prov |>
  transmute(measurement_type, canonical = is_canonical, units,
            method, accuracy, from = year_started, to = year_ended) |>
  datatable(
    caption  = paste("CTD measurement provenance — instrument, stated accuracy and",
                     "era, from the CalCOFI hydrographic master's 0-Measurements"),
    rownames = FALSE,
    options  = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE, dom = "ftip"))
NoteDocumentation only, for now

This table is rendered, not written into metadata.json. Promoting it into the sidecar so consumers get instrument provenance alongside units is a follow-up that belongs in calcofi4db::build_metadata_json(), and 18 of the 35 era rows still need a data manager to confirm their mapping to canonical types (hydro_master_06).

24.4 Drop intermediate table

Code 
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ctd_raw")

25 Measurement Frequency

ctd_measurement is by far the largest table in this dataset — in the prior release the calcofi_ctd-cast parquet totaled 22.16 GB, with ctd_measurement alone at 15.8 GB (233 M rows). Three stacked multipliers drive that size. The queries below quantify each, motivating the adaptively-thinned ctd_thin table built in the next section.

Code 
freq_tbl_sizes <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT 'ctd_cast'         AS table_name, COUNT(*) AS n_rows FROM ctd_cast
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'ctd_measurement' AS table_name, COUNT(*) AS n_rows FROM ctd_measurement
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'ctd_summary'     AS table_name, COUNT(*) AS n_rows FROM ctd_summary")

n_meas_rows <- freq_tbl_sizes$n_rows[freq_tbl_sizes$table_name == "ctd_measurement"]
cat(glue("ctd_measurement: {format(n_meas_rows, big.mark = ',')} rows"), "\n")

freq_tbl_sizes |>
  dt(caption = "Normalized CTD table row counts (this run)",
     fname   = "ctd_freq_table_sizes")

25.1 Multiplier 1 — sub-meter depth resolution

CTD profiles record a sample roughly every metre from surface to seafloor (~3,600 m max). Thinning to a 10 m grid is therefore an order-of-magnitude reduction on the depth axis.

Code 
# depth interval between consecutive samples within a cast, using `pressure`
# as a representative measurement_type (all types share a cast's depth grid)
freq_depth_int <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  WITH gaps AS (
    SELECT depth_m - LAG(depth_m) OVER (
             PARTITION BY ctd_cast_uuid ORDER BY depth_m) AS d_gap
    FROM ctd_measurement
    WHERE measurement_type = 'pressure')
  SELECT
    ROUND(MIN(d_gap), 2)                 AS min_m,
    ROUND(QUANTILE_CONT(d_gap, 0.25), 2) AS q25_m,
    ROUND(MEDIAN(d_gap), 2)              AS median_m,
    ROUND(QUANTILE_CONT(d_gap, 0.75), 2) AS q75_m,
    ROUND(MAX(d_gap), 2)                 AS max_m
  FROM gaps
  WHERE d_gap IS NOT NULL")

cat(glue(
  "median within-cast depth interval: {freq_depth_int$median_m} m ",
  "(~{round(10 / freq_depth_int$median_m)}x reduction at a 10 m grid)"), "\n")

freq_depth_int |>
  dt(caption = "Within-cast depth interval (m), representative type `pressure`",
     fname   = "ctd_freq_depth_resolution")

25.2 Multiplier 2 — up- and down-casts both stored

Nearly every physical cast is recorded as a separate down-cast and up-cast. Keeping a single direction roughly halves the rows.

Code 
# physical cast = (cruise_key, site_key, cast_base); direction resolved from
# cast_dir, falling back to the cast_key suffix (trailing d/u)
freq_cast_dir <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  WITH phys AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      cruise_key, site_key,
      regexp_replace(cast_key, '[duDU]$', '') AS cast_base,
      COALESCE(
        cast_dir,
        CASE
          WHEN RIGHT(cast_key, 1) IN ('d', 'D') THEN 'D'
          WHEN RIGHT(cast_key, 1) IN ('u', 'U') THEN 'U'
        END) AS dir
    FROM ctd_cast)
  SELECT
    COUNT(DISTINCT cruise_key || '|' || site_key || '|' || cast_base)
                                       AS n_physical_casts,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE dir = 'D')   AS n_with_downcast,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE dir = 'U')   AS n_with_upcast,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE dir IS NULL) AS n_unknown_dir
  FROM phys")

cat(glue(
  "{format(freq_cast_dir$n_physical_casts, big.mark = ',')} physical casts; ",
  "{format(freq_cast_dir$n_with_downcast, big.mark = ',')} have a downcast, ",
  "{format(freq_cast_dir$n_with_upcast, big.mark = ',')} an upcast"), "\n")

freq_cast_dir |>
  dt(caption = "Cast direction coverage per physical cast",
     fname   = "ctd_freq_cast_direction")

25.3 Multiplier 3 — redundant measurement-type variants

Many of the measurement types below are variants of the same property (multiple oxygen units and sensor/correction combinations, dual temperature and salinity sensors, derived estimates). ctd_thin keeps the canonical types — the averages, the bottle references, the uncorrected sensors (2026-08-06, so a sensor-only cruise still has salinity and oxygen) and, since 2026-09-10, the bottle-corrected per-sensor series and the chlorophyll / nitrate sensor estimates at both correction levels (Rasmus Swalethorp’s transect-plotter rule) — see the is_canonical flag in metadata/measurement_type.csv, set by libs/build_ctd_measurement_registry.R.

Code 
freq_meas_types <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
    measurement_type,
    COUNT(*)                      AS n_rows,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ctd_cast_uuid) AS n_casts
  FROM ctd_measurement
  GROUP BY measurement_type
  ORDER BY n_rows DESC")

cat(glue(
  "{nrow(freq_meas_types)} distinct measurement_type values in ctd_measurement"),
  "\n")

freq_meas_types |>
  dt(caption = "Rows per measurement_type",
     fname   = "ctd_freq_measurement_types")

26 CTD Thin

ctd_thin is an adaptively-thinned ctd_measurement: one cast direction per physical cast, canonical measurement types only, and a ~10 m depth grid with thermocline / halocline inflections preserved via Ramer–Douglas–Peucker line simplification. It is the headline CTD table; full ctd_measurement is retained as a supplemental output. See the Measurement Frequency section above for the size rationale.

26.1 Verify cast pairing

Code 
# physical cast = (cruise_key, site_key, cast_base); direction comes from the
# cast_key suffix (trailing d/u), which is part of the deterministic
# ctd_cast_uuid key and fully consistent per cast. confirm casts are paired
# before thinning by direction.
ctd_pairing <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  WITH phys AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      cruise_key, site_key,
      regexp_replace(cast_key, '[duDU]$', '') AS cast_base,
      CASE WHEN RIGHT(cast_key, 1) IN ('d', 'D') THEN 'D'
           WHEN RIGHT(cast_key, 1) IN ('u', 'U') THEN 'U' END AS dir
    FROM ctd_cast)
  SELECT n_dirs, COUNT(*) AS n_physical_casts
  FROM (
    SELECT cruise_key, site_key, cast_base, COUNT(DISTINCT dir) AS n_dirs
    FROM phys GROUP BY 1, 2, 3)
  GROUP BY n_dirs ORDER BY n_dirs")

n_paired <- sum(ctd_pairing$n_physical_casts[ctd_pairing$n_dirs == 2])
n_single <- sum(ctd_pairing$n_physical_casts[ctd_pairing$n_dirs == 1])
cat(glue(
  "{format(n_paired, big.mark = ',')} physical casts have both directions, ",
  "{format(n_single, big.mark = ',')} have one"), "\n")

# sanity: most casts should be paired — a near-zero n_paired means the pairing
# key is wrong and the single-direction lever would silently keep everything
stopifnot(
  "ctd_thin: cast pairing key looks wrong (no two-direction casts)" =
    n_paired > n_single)

ctd_pairing |>
  dt(caption = "Cast directions per physical cast", fname = "ctd_thin_pairing")

26.2 Choose a single cast direction

Code 
# canonical measurement types for ctd_thin (one per property; see is_canonical
# in metadata/measurement_type.csv)
canon_types <- d_meas_type |>
  filter(str_detect(`_source_datasets`, "calcofi_ctd-cast"), is_canonical) |>
  pull(measurement_type)
canon_in <- paste0("'", canon_types, "'", collapse = ", ")
cat(glue("{length(canon_types)} canonical measurement types: ",
         "{paste(canon_types, collapse = ', ')}"), "\n")

# choose one direction per physical cast: prefer downcast, fall back to upcast.
# _chosen_dir maps every chosen-direction ctd_cast_uuid to its physical cast
# (phys_cast_id) and direction.
dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE _chosen_dir AS
  WITH resolved AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      ctd_cast_uuid, cruise_key, site_key, cast_key,
      regexp_replace(cast_key, '[duDU]$', '') AS cast_base,
      CASE WHEN RIGHT(cast_key, 1) IN ('d', 'D') THEN 'D'
           WHEN RIGHT(cast_key, 1) IN ('u', 'U') THEN 'U' END AS dir
    FROM ctd_cast),
  pick AS (
    SELECT cruise_key, site_key, cast_base, cast_key, dir
    FROM (SELECT DISTINCT cruise_key, site_key, cast_base, cast_key, dir
          FROM resolved)
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY cruise_key, site_key, cast_base
      ORDER BY CASE dir WHEN 'D' THEN 1 WHEN 'U' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END,
               cast_key) = 1)
  SELECT
    r.ctd_cast_uuid,
    r.cruise_key,
    r.cruise_key || '|' || r.site_key || '|' || r.cast_base AS phys_cast_id,
    p.dir AS cast_dir
  FROM resolved r
  JOIN pick p USING (cruise_key, site_key, cast_base, cast_key)")

n_chosen <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM _chosen_dir")$n
cat(glue("_chosen_dir: {format(n_chosen, big.mark = ',')} cast records ",
         "(single direction per physical cast)"), "\n")

26.3 10 m depth grid

Code 
# depth backbone: every distinct depth a canonical measurement is recorded at,
# per chosen-direction physical cast
dbExecute(con, glue("
  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE _profile_depths AS
  SELECT DISTINCT cd.phys_cast_id, m.depth_m
  FROM ctd_measurement m
  JOIN _chosen_dir cd ON m.ctd_cast_uuid = cd.ctd_cast_uuid
  WHERE m.measurement_type IN ({canon_in})"))

# 10 m grid: the sample nearest each 10 m node per profile, plus the shallowest
# and deepest sample (RDP needs fixed profile endpoints)
dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE _grid_depths AS
  WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT phys_cast_id, depth_m,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY phys_cast_id, ROUND(depth_m / 10.0) * 10.0
        ORDER BY ABS(depth_m - ROUND(depth_m / 10.0) * 10.0), depth_m) AS rn
    FROM _profile_depths),
  endpoints AS (
    SELECT phys_cast_id, MIN(depth_m) AS depth_m FROM _profile_depths GROUP BY 1
    UNION
    SELECT phys_cast_id, MAX(depth_m) AS depth_m FROM _profile_depths GROUP BY 1)
  SELECT phys_cast_id, depth_m FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1
  UNION
  SELECT phys_cast_id, depth_m FROM endpoints")

n_prof <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM _profile_depths")$n
n_grid <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM _grid_depths")$n
cat(glue("_grid_depths: {format(n_grid, big.mark = ',')} depths on the 10 m grid ",
         "(from {format(n_prof, big.mark = ',')} profile depths)"), "\n")

26.4 Inflection points (Ramer–Douglas–Peucker)

Code 
# Ramer-Douglas-Peucker line simplification: keep depths where a profile deviates
# from the local straight line by more than `eps` (captures thermocline /
# halocline inflections). pure DP — the ~10 m backbone is provided separately by
# _grid_depths, so RDP only adds genuine inflections on top of it.
rdp_keep <- function(x, y, eps) {
  n    <- length(x)
  keep <- rep(FALSE, n)
  if (n == 0L) return(keep)
  keep[c(1L, n)] <- TRUE
  if (n <= 2L) return(keep)
  stack <- list(c(1L, n))
  while (length(stack) > 0L) {
    seg   <- stack[[length(stack)]]
    stack[[length(stack)]] <- NULL
    i <- seg[1L]; j <- seg[2L]
    if (j - i < 2L) next
    idx <- (i + 1L):(j - 1L)
    dx  <- x[j] - x[i]
    dy  <- y[j] - y[i]
    den <- sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
    d <- if (den == 0) {
      abs(y[idx] - y[i])
    } else {
      abs(dy * x[idx] - dx * y[idx] + x[j] * y[i] - y[j] * x[i]) / den
    }
    if (max(d) > eps) {
      k <- idx[which.max(d)]
      keep[k] <- TRUE
      stack[[length(stack) + 1L]] <- c(i, k)
      stack[[length(stack) + 1L]] <- c(k, j)
    }
  }
  keep
}

# per-variable tolerance in measurement units — the primary tuning knob, set so
# the median retained-sample gap lands near the 10 m grid spacing (a looser eps
# keeps fewer inflections; revisit with the spot-check in the verification section)
rdp_eps <- c(temperature_ave = 0.2, salinity_ave_corr = 0.04)

# run RDP per cruise to keep memory flat: pull the two key variables for
# chosen-direction casts, simplify each profile, collect retained depths
cruise_keys <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DISTINCT cruise_key FROM _chosen_dir")$cruise_key

rdp_retained <- purrr::map(cruise_keys, function(ck) {
  d_prof <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
    SELECT cd.phys_cast_id, m.measurement_type, m.depth_m,
           AVG(m.measurement_value) AS measurement_value
    FROM ctd_measurement m
    JOIN _chosen_dir cd
      ON m.ctd_cast_uuid = cd.ctd_cast_uuid AND cd.cruise_key = '{ck}'
    WHERE m.cruise_key = '{ck}'
      AND m.measurement_type IN ('temperature_ave', 'salinity_ave_corr')
      AND m.measurement_value IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY cd.phys_cast_id, m.measurement_type, m.depth_m"))
  if (nrow(d_prof) == 0) return(NULL)
  d_prof |>
    arrange(phys_cast_id, measurement_type, depth_m) |>
    group_by(phys_cast_id, measurement_type) |>
    filter(rdp_keep(depth_m, measurement_value,
                    eps = rdp_eps[[measurement_type[1]]])) |>
    ungroup() |>
    distinct(phys_cast_id, depth_m)
}) |>
  purrr::list_rbind() |>
  distinct(phys_cast_id, depth_m)

dbWriteTable(con, "_rdp_retained", rdp_retained,
             temporary = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)
cat(glue("_rdp_retained: {format(nrow(rdp_retained), big.mark = ',')} ",
         "(profile, depth) pairs flagged as inflections"), "\n")

26.5 Assemble ctd_thin

Code 
# Union three retention reasons, in precedence order: 10 m grid, RDP inflections,
# then bottle-trip depths.
#
# The third is why this section changed. Thinning is designed for DENSE SENSOR
# SCANS: the 10 m backbone and the RDP inflections are both derived from
# temperature/salinity profiles, so a depth is kept because the *sensor* profile
# bends there. Bottle values are not a profile — they are a handful of discrete,
# lab-analysed samples per cast at depths chosen by the watch, and nothing about
# the sensor profile knows where they are. Selecting depths by sensor geometry and
# then subsetting bottle values to those depths silently discards most of them.
#
# Measured against release v2026.07.17: of 133,206 distinct (cast, depth) bottle
# ammonium measurements, only 35,549 (26.7%) sit at a depth this logic retained.
# Roughly half the loss is the cast-direction choice (by design); the rest was
# depth thinning throwing away real lab samples. So flagging btl_ammonium as
# canonical is necessary but NOT sufficient — without this clause it would have
# landed about a quarter of the ammonium record in `obs` and looked like success.
#
# A bottle depth costs nothing to keep (a few rows per cast) and cannot be
# reconstructed by interpolation, so retain every one carrying a canonical value.
canon_btl <- d_meas_ctd |>
  filter(is_canonical, str_starts(measurement_type, "btl_") |
           measurement_type %in% c("salinity_btl", "oxygen_btl_ml_l",
                                   "oxygen_btl_umol_kg")) |>
  pull(measurement_type)
say(glue("bottle-grain canonical types retained whole: ",
         "{if (length(canon_btl)) paste(canon_btl, collapse = ', ') else '(none)'}"))

btl_clause <- if (length(canon_btl)) glue("
  UNION
  SELECT cd.phys_cast_id, m.depth_m, 'bottle' AS retained_reason
  FROM ctd_measurement m
  JOIN _chosen_dir cd ON m.ctd_cast_uuid = cd.ctd_cast_uuid
  WHERE m.measurement_type IN ({paste(sprintf(\"'%s'\", canon_btl), collapse = ', ')})
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM _grid_depths g
      WHERE g.phys_cast_id = cd.phys_cast_id AND g.depth_m = m.depth_m)
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM _rdp_retained r
      WHERE r.phys_cast_id = cd.phys_cast_id AND r.depth_m = m.depth_m)") else ""

dbExecute(con, glue("
  CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE _retained_depths AS
  SELECT phys_cast_id, depth_m, 'grid' AS retained_reason FROM _grid_depths
  UNION
  SELECT r.phys_cast_id, r.depth_m, 'inflection' AS retained_reason
  FROM _rdp_retained r
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM _grid_depths g
    WHERE g.phys_cast_id = r.phys_cast_id AND g.depth_m = r.depth_m)
  {btl_clause}"))

# ctd_thin: ctd_measurement rows that are a canonical type, on the chosen
# direction, at a retained depth — a pure row subset (values never interpolated).
# the QUALIFY de-dups defensively on (ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m, measurement_type):
# the dedup_ctd_raw chunk above already makes ctd_measurement unique, so this is
# a no-op safeguard that keeps ctd_thin's PK guaranteed-unique on its own.
dbExecute(con, glue("
  CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ctd_thin AS
  WITH candidates AS (
    SELECT
      m.ctd_cast_uuid,
      m.depth_m,
      m.measurement_type,
      m.measurement_value,
      m.measurement_qual,
      cd.cast_dir,
      rd.retained_reason,
      m.cruise_key
    FROM ctd_measurement m
    JOIN _chosen_dir cd      ON m.ctd_cast_uuid = cd.ctd_cast_uuid
    JOIN _retained_depths rd ON rd.phys_cast_id = cd.phys_cast_id
                            AND rd.depth_m      = m.depth_m
    WHERE m.measurement_type IN ({canon_in}))
  SELECT *
  FROM candidates
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY ctd_cast_uuid, depth_m, measurement_type
    ORDER BY measurement_qual NULLS LAST, measurement_value) = 1
  ORDER BY cruise_key, ctd_cast_uuid, measurement_type, depth_m"))

n_thin <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_thin")$n
n_meas <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_measurement")$n
cat(glue(
  "ctd_thin: {format(n_thin, big.mark = ',')} rows ",
  "({round(100 * n_thin / n_meas, 1)}% of ctd_measurement's ",
  "{format(n_meas, big.mark = ',')})"), "\n")

# deterministic PK from the natural key, mirroring ctd_measurement
assign_deterministic_uuids_md5(
  con        = con,
  table_name = "ctd_thin",
  id_col     = "ctd_thin_uuid",
  key_cols   = c("ctd_cast_uuid", "depth_m", "measurement_type"))

# drop scratch tables; _chosen_dir is kept for the verification chunk that
# follows and dropped there (downstream metadata helpers enumerate all DB tables)
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _profile_depths")
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _grid_depths")
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _rdp_retained")
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS _retained_depths")

26.6 Verify ctd_thin

Code 
# 1. row count + thinning ratio
n_thin <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_thin")$n
n_meas <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_measurement")$n
cat(glue("ctd_thin: {format(n_thin, big.mark = ',')} rows = ",
         "{round(100 * n_thin / n_meas, 1)}% of ctd_measurement"), "\n")
stopifnot(
  "ctd_thin is empty"                          = n_thin > 0,
  "ctd_thin not smaller than ctd_measurement"  = n_thin < n_meas)

# 2. measurement_type is a subset of the canonical list
thin_types <- dbGetQuery(con,
  "SELECT DISTINCT measurement_type FROM ctd_thin")$measurement_type
stopifnot("ctd_thin has non-canonical measurement_type" =
  length(setdiff(thin_types, canon_types)) == 0)

# 3. ctd_thin_uuid is unique
stopifnot("ctd_thin_uuid not unique" = dbGetQuery(con,
  "SELECT COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT ctd_thin_uuid) AS n FROM ctd_thin")$n == 0)

# 4. faithful subset of ctd_measurement — every ctd_thin row corresponds to a
#    real ctd_measurement row with the same value (thinning selects rows, never
#    interpolates). a NOT EXISTS check, since ctd_measurement has duplicate keys.
stopifnot("ctd_thin rows not a faithful subset of ctd_measurement" =
  dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS n
    FROM ctd_thin t
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM ctd_measurement m
      WHERE m.ctd_cast_uuid     = t.ctd_cast_uuid
        AND m.depth_m           = t.depth_m
        AND m.measurement_type  = t.measurement_type
        AND m.measurement_value IS NOT DISTINCT FROM t.measurement_value)")$n == 0)

# 5. retained_reason populated with the expected categories. 'bottle' joins
#    'grid'/'inflection' only when a canonical bottle-grain type exists (see the
#    assemble chunk), so it is required conditionally rather than always.
reason_breakdown <- dbGetQuery(con,
  "SELECT retained_reason, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT depth_m) AS n_depths
   FROM ctd_thin GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC")
expected_reasons <- c("grid", "inflection", if (length(canon_btl)) "bottle")
stopifnot(
  "ctd_thin retained_reason has unexpected values" =
    all(reason_breakdown$retained_reason %in% expected_reasons),
  "ctd_thin retained_reason missing a category" =
    all(expected_reasons %in% reason_breakdown$retained_reason))
# previously computed only for the assertion and never shown
say("retained_reason breakdown:")
print(reason_breakdown)

# 5b. the point of the 'bottle' reason: every canonical bottle-grain measurement on
#     a chosen-direction cast must survive thinning, not just those that happened to
#     land on a sensor-derived depth. Assert 100% retention rather than trusting it.
if (length(canon_btl)) {
  btl_in <- paste(sprintf("'%s'", canon_btl), collapse = ", ")
  btl_cov <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
    WITH avail AS (
      SELECT m.ctd_cast_uuid, m.depth_m, m.measurement_type
      FROM ctd_measurement m JOIN _chosen_dir cd USING (ctd_cast_uuid)
      WHERE m.measurement_type IN ({btl_in}))
    SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM avail) AS available,
           (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ctd_thin WHERE measurement_type IN ({btl_in})) AS retained"))
  say(glue("bottle-grain canonical: {format(btl_cov$retained, big.mark = ',')} of ",
           "{format(btl_cov$available, big.mark = ',')} retained ",
           "({round(100 * btl_cov$retained / btl_cov$available, 1)}%)"))
  stopifnot("every canonical bottle measurement on the chosen direction must be retained" =
              btl_cov$retained == btl_cov$available)
}

# 6. one cast direction per physical cast; no physical cast dropped entirely
coverage <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("
  WITH meas_casts AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT cd.phys_cast_id
    FROM ctd_measurement m
    JOIN _chosen_dir cd ON m.ctd_cast_uuid = cd.ctd_cast_uuid
    WHERE m.measurement_type IN ({canon_in})),
  thin AS (
    SELECT cd.phys_cast_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.cast_dir) AS n_dir
    FROM ctd_thin t
    JOIN _chosen_dir cd ON t.ctd_cast_uuid = cd.ctd_cast_uuid
    GROUP BY cd.phys_cast_id)
  SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM thin)                  AS n_thin_casts,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM thin WHERE n_dir > 1)  AS n_multi_dir,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
       SELECT phys_cast_id FROM meas_casts
       EXCEPT
       SELECT phys_cast_id FROM thin))           AS n_dropped"))
stopifnot(
  "ctd_thin: physical cast with >1 direction" = coverage$n_multi_dir == 0,
  "ctd_thin: physical cast dropped entirely"  = coverage$n_dropped   == 0)
