```{r}
cache_csv <- file.path(dir_meta, "ctd_zip_urls.csv")

d_zips_web <- tryCatch(
  {
    d <- read_html(url) |>
      html_nodes("a[href$='.zip']") |>
      html_attr("href") |>
      tibble(url = _) |>
      mutate(
        url = if_else(
          str_starts(url, "http"),
          url,
          paste0("https://calcofi.org", url)
        ),
        file_zip = basename(url),
        # year comes from the URL directory (/downloads/2026/), which is
        # authoritative for a published zip; month from the cruise code
        year = str_extract(url, "/(\\d{4})/", group = 1) |> as.integer(),
        month = str_extract(url, "-\\d{2}(\\d{2})", group = 1) |> as.integer()
      ) |>
      add_zip_meta()
    write_csv(d, cache_csv)
    say(glue("Scraped {nrow(d)} zip URLs from {url}"))
    d
  },
  error = function(e) {
    if (file_exists(cache_csv)) {
      say(glue("Website unavailable, using cached URLs from {cache_csv}"))
      read_csv(cache_csv, show_col_types = FALSE)
    } else {
      stop(e)
    }
  }
) |>
  mutate(source = "web")

# --- source 2: zips on disk that calcofi.org does not publish ------------------
# `url` is deliberately NA: there is nothing to download, the file is already in
# dir_dl (put there by prime_zips_from_gcs above, or by hand). download_and_unzip()
# reads that NA as "already local, unzip only".
#
# year/month are parsed from the FILENAME here rather than a URL path. The two
# agree wherever both exist (20-2601RL → /downloads/2026/, 2026-01), but a local
# zip has no URL to read them from. Web rows keep the URL derivation so no
# currently-published value changes.
# a Shared-Drive drop is classified by its CONTENTS, a calcofi.org link by its name: the fall
# 2026 in-cruise drop `20-2611_CTDCast.zip` (Rasmus Swalethorp, 2026-11-04) holds the bottle-merged
# 1 m-binned `20-2611_CTDBTL_001-011D.csv` / `…U.csv` under a name the rule above reads as a
# raw-cast archive, which download_and_unzip() never opens. A local archive whose members are db
# products is a preliminary drop whatever its name; the central directory is one seek per archive
# (utils::unzip, not the masked zip::unzip — see [jrw_overlap_report]). Only `raw`-named local
# archives are inspected, so the JRW finals and the Prelim drops keep their name rule.
zip_holds_db_csvs <- function(file_zip) {
  members <- tryCatch(utils::unzip(file.path(dir_dl, file_zip), list = TRUE)$Name,
                      error = function(e) character(0))
  any(str_detect(members, "_CTD(BTL)?_\\d{3}-\\d{3}[DU]\\.csv$"))
}
d_zips_local <- tibble(
  file_zip = list.files(dir_dl, pattern = "\\.zip$")) |>
  anti_join(d_zips_web, by = "file_zip") |>
  add_zip_meta() |>
  mutate(
    zip_by_content = zip_type == "raw" & map_lgl(file_zip, zip_holds_db_csvs),
    zip_type       = if_else(zip_by_content, "preliminary", zip_type),
    url    = NA_character_,
    # "19-" / "20-" gives the century, "YYMM" the rest
    year   = as.integer(str_extract(file_zip, "^(\\d{2})", group = 1)) * 100L +
             as.integer(str_extract(file_zip, "^\\d{2}-(\\d{2})", group = 1)),
    month  = as.integer(str_extract(file_zip, "^\\d{2}-\\d{2}(\\d{2})", group = 1)),
    source = "gcs") |>
  select(url, file_zip, year, month, cruise_key, zip_type, source, zip_by_content)
if (any(d_zips_local$zip_by_content))
  say(glue("Preliminary by contents (a raw-named Shared-Drive drop holding db CSVs): ",
           "{paste(d_zips_local$file_zip[d_zips_local$zip_by_content], collapse = ', ')}"))

d_zips <- bind_rows(d_zips_web, d_zips_local) |>
  arrange(desc(year), desc(month), file_zip)

stopifnot(!any(d_zips$zip_type == "unknown"))

say(glue("Zip inventory: {nrow(d_zips)} ",
         "({sum(d_zips$source == 'web')} calcofi.org, ",
         "{sum(d_zips$source == 'gcs')} Shared Drive only)"))

d_zips |>
  mutate(
    file_zip = if_else(
      is.na(url), file_zip, glue("<a href={url}>{file_zip}</a>"))
  ) |>
  select(-url) |>
  dt(
    caption = "All zip files in the inventory",
    fname = "ctd_zip_files",
    escape = F
  )
```

## Check for Resumable State

The heavy path here — download, parse, pivot — is about an hour, and this notebook
is re-rendered mostly for reasons that have nothing to do with its inputs: a
narrative edit, a new diagnostic, a corrected sentence. Paying an hour to prove
that nothing changed is what stops a pipeline notebook being usable as a living
document, so the decision is made on evidence rather than on a flag: **skip the
heavy path when the parquet outputs are complete and the inputs they were built
from still fingerprint the same.**

The inputs are the published zip URL list scraped above, plus the metadata
registries that steer the pivot. `calcofi4db::input_fingerprint()` hashes them and
records the result beside the wrangling database; a *missing* input hashes as
`<missing>` rather than being skipped, so deleting a corrections file invalidates
the outputs instead of reading as "no change".

When the heavy path is skipped, **every chunk from here to the GCS upload is
displayed but not evaluated** — their code is still the record of how the tables
were built, but the tables themselves are not rebuilt, so those sections show no
output. The [Findings](#findings) section at the end reads the **parquet** rather
than the wrangling database and therefore always runs; that is what makes this
worth doing, and what keeps a skipped render honest rather than merely quiet.

```{r}
#| label: check_resume

# `overwrite` in libs/ingest.R is TRUE for every ingest and cannot be flipped
# globally — the comment there records that trying it broke a different notebook,
# because the skip path is not uniformly safe. So this notebook decides for itself.
# CTD_FORCE_REBUILD=TRUE (or overwrite_all) runs the heavy path regardless.
fingerprint_path <- here(glue("data/wrangling/{dir_label}_inputs.json"))

# kept OUT of dir_parquet on purpose: sync_to_gcs() mirrors that directory to a
# world-readable bucket, and this is local state about one machine's outputs.
fp <- input_fingerprint(
  # ONLY inputs that can change the OUTPUTS belong here. measurement_qual.csv is
  # deliberately absent: it is a vocabulary the diagnostics decode against, never
  # something the pivot reads, so hashing it would force an hour of rebuild for a
  # documentation edit that cannot alter a single row.
  files = c(
    here("metadata/measurement_type.csv"),
    here("metadata/core_dictionary.csv"),
    file.path(dir_meta, "flds_redefine.csv"),
    file.path(dir_meta, "tbls_redefine.csv"),
    file.path(dir_meta, "cruise_key_corrections.csv"),
    file.path(dir_meta, "flag_overrides.csv"),
    file.path(dir_meta, "metadata_derived.csv")),
  # the engine version is an input too: a change to calcofi4db's projection or
  # parsing would otherwise leave the fingerprint identical and keep outputs that
  # the current code would no longer produce
  #
  # keyed on source+filename, NOT on `url`: a Shared-Drive-only zip has no URL, so
  # hashing `d_zips$url` would let the whole Wilkinson archive (and 2607SH) arrive
  # without invalidating anything — the run would report "inputs unchanged" and
  # skip the rebuild that was the entire point.
  #
  # ...and the archive's SIZE on disk: a provider re-publishing a corrected zip under
  # the same name (20-2607SH_CTDPrelim.zip, 2026-09-14: station numbers >= 100 had
  # been cut to three digits) changes nothing else, so without it the fix would read
  # as "inputs unchanged" and never be ingested (CalCOFI/workflows#104)
  values = c(sort(paste(d_zips$source, d_zips$file_zip,
                        file.size(file.path(dir_dl, d_zips$file_zip)))),
             paste0("calcofi4db ", as.character(packageVersion("calcofi4db")))))
fp_prior <- read_input_fingerprint(fingerprint_path)
fp_same  <- !is.null(fp_prior) && identical(fp_prior$hash, fp$hash)

# parquet is "complete" when every non-supplemental manifest table is on disk
parquet_ok    <- FALSE
manifest_path <- file.path(dir_parquet, "manifest.json")
if (file_exists(manifest_path)) {
  mf       <- jsonlite::read_json(manifest_path)
  expected <- setdiff(mf$tables, unlist(mf$supplemental))
  parquet_ok <- all(vapply(expected, function(tbl) {
    file_exists(file.path(dir_stage, paste0(tbl, ".parquet"))) ||
      dir_exists(file.path(dir_stage, tbl))
  }, logical(1)))
}

force_rebuild <- overwrite_all ||
  isTRUE(as.logical(Sys.getenv("CTD_FORCE_REBUILD", "FALSE")))
parquet_complete <- parquet_ok && fp_same && !force_rebuild

if (parquet_complete) {
  say(glue(
    "Inputs unchanged and parquet complete ({length(mf$tables)} tables, ",
    "{format(mf$total_rows, big.mark = ',')} rows) — ",
    "skipping download/parse/pivot"))
  say(glue("  fingerprint {substr(fp$hash, 1, 12)}, recorded {fp_prior$recorded_at}"))
} else if (force_rebuild) {
  say("Rebuilding: forced (CTD_FORCE_REBUILD / overwrite_all)")
} else if (parquet_ok && !fp_same) {
  say("Rebuilding: inputs changed since the recorded fingerprint —")
  for (f in changed_inputs(fp, fp_prior)) say(glue("  {f}"))
} else {
  say("Rebuilding: no complete parquet output found")
}

# --- only now touch anything -------------------------------------------------
# overwrite keeps the checkpoint DB, the downloads, and (importantly) dir_parquet,
# so write_parquet_outputs() can content-hash dedup against the prior run and only
# changed partitions are re-written and re-uploaded.
if (overwrite && !parquet_complete) {
  if (file_exists(db_path)) file_delete(db_path)
  # clear any stale WAL/tmp from an interrupted run so the restored checkpoint
  # DB opens cleanly (avoids "WAL checkpoint iteration does not match" errors)
  db_wal <- paste0(db_path, ".wal")
  db_tmp <- paste0(db_path, ".tmp")
  if (file_exists(db_wal)) file_delete(db_wal)
  if (dir_exists(db_tmp))  dir_delete(db_tmp)
  if (overwrite_all) {
    if (dir_exists(dir_parquet))    dir_delete(dir_parquet)
    if (dir_exists(dir_stage))      dir_delete(dir_stage)
    if (file_exists(db_checkpoint)) file_delete(db_checkpoint)
    rds_files <- list.files(dir_tmp, pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
    if (length(rds_files) > 0) file_delete(rds_files)
    say("Deleted parquet, checkpoint DB, and RDS intermediates")
  }
}

# restore from checkpoint DB if available (skips expensive read+bind+filter) — but
# only a checkpoint built from THESE archives: it holds ctd_raw, i.e. the files as
# read, so a replaced archive must not be answered from the old copy of it
fp_zips <- input_fingerprint(
  files  = file.path(dir_meta, "flds_redefine.csv"),
  values = sort(paste(d_zips$file_zip, file.size(file.path(dir_dl, d_zips$file_zip)))))
checkpoint_fp_path <- paste0(db_checkpoint, ".inputs.json")
fp_ckpt <- read_input_fingerprint(checkpoint_fp_path)
if (file_exists(db_checkpoint) &&
    (is.null(fp_ckpt) || !identical(fp_ckpt$hash, fp_zips$hash))) {
  file_delete(db_checkpoint)
  say("Checkpoint discarded: built from a different set of archives")
}
if (!parquet_complete && file_exists(db_checkpoint) && !file_exists(db_path)) {
  file_copy(db_checkpoint, db_path, overwrite = TRUE)
  say(glue("Restored from checkpoint: {db_checkpoint}"))
}

con <- get_duckdb_con(db_path)
load_duckdb_extension(con, "spatial")
load_duckdb_extension(con, "icu")

# DuckDB's memory limit from what is AVAILABLE, not half of total: this notebook
# shares the machine with R's own ~20 GB of scan frames and whatever else runs (the
# 2026-09-23 run crawled at 3-9x under swap with a fixed half-of-RAM limit). 40 % of
# available, between 2 GB and half of total; DuckDB spills to temp_directory beyond it.
# BUILD_MEMORY_GB overrides it (as libs/duckdb_budget.R does in the sibling repos): on
# 2026-09-24 availability was 5.8 GB at start, so this rule gave DuckDB 2 GB while R itself
# held ~25 GB of scan frames that nothing released (fixed in [rename_fields]).
mem_sys <- ps::ps_system_memory()
mem_gb  <- max(2, floor(min(mem_sys$total / 2, mem_sys$avail * 0.4) / 1024^3))
mem_env <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Sys.getenv("BUILD_MEMORY_GB", NA)))
if (!is.na(mem_env) && mem_env > 0) mem_gb <- mem_env
say(glue("DuckDB memory_limit {mem_gb} GB (available {round(mem_sys$avail / 1024^3, 1)} of ",
         "{round(mem_sys$total / 1024^3)} GB; BUILD_MEMORY_GB {if (is.na(mem_env)) 'unset' else mem_env})"))
# every connection this notebook opens to the wrangling DB gets the same budget. The
# checkpoint step closes and reopens `con`, and until 2026-09-24 the reopened connection
# silently ran on DuckDB's default (80 % of RAM) instead of this limit: the restarted
# render's R process peaked at 22 GB in [ctd_measurement] with a 6 GB limit "set".
# preserve_insertion_order = false lets the large INSERT ... SELECTs of the pivot stream
# instead of buffering to keep row order, which nothing downstream relies on (every
# table is re-sorted at write_parquet_outputs()).
duck_budget <- function(con) {
  dbExecute(con, glue("SET memory_limit = '{mem_gb}GB'"))
  dbExecute(con, glue("SET temp_directory = '{dir_tmp}'"))
  dbExecute(con, "SET preserve_insertion_order = false")
  invisible(con)
}
duck_budget(con)

# a second, cheaper resume: ctd_raw already pivoted from a prior interrupted run
has_ctd_raw <- FALSE
if (!parquet_complete) {
  has_ctd_raw <- "ctd_raw" %in% DBI::dbListTables(con)
  if (has_ctd_raw) {
    n_raw <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ctd_raw")$n
    say(glue(
      "Checkpoint: ctd_raw already loaded ",
      "({format(n_raw, big.mark = ',')} rows) — ",
      "skipping read+bind+filter"))
  }
}

# set eval for read+bind+filter chunks
skip_read_bind <- parquet_complete || has_ctd_raw
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = !skip_read_bind)
```

## Choose Which Archives to Read

Jim Wilkinson's archive and calcofi.org overlap on 66 cruises, and **130 of the 140
comparable files are identical** — `20-0302JD_CTDBTL_001-100D.csv` from
`20-0302JD_CTDFinalDB.zip` is md5-identical to calcofi.org's copy inside
`20-0302JD_CTDFinalQC.zip`, and so are the great majority of the rest. But **8 files
across 4 cruises are not** (`1810SR`, `1501NH`, `1604SH`, `1607OS`), so this is a
preference, not an equivalence.

`calcofi.org wins where both publish a final.` It is the citable published source,
it is what the existing 66 cruises in the release were already built from, and
switching them would rewrite years of released data on the strength of an
undocumented difference. The Shared Drive archive is read **only** for the cruises
calcofi.org has no final for — which is also what keeps the ~1 hr heavy path from
doubling to parse duplicates.

The archive is still mirrored **completely** to GCS (0.89 GB): it is the basis for
any future backfill of calcofi.org, and for answering the question below.

::: {.callout-important title="Where the two sources disagree, and why it is a provider question"}
The `jrw_overlap_report` chunk below compares every overlapping archive and lists
the disagreements rather than asserting they cannot happen — an earlier draft
asserted byte-identity and was wrong.

The clearest case is **1810SR**, where the Shared Drive copy is **2.1× the size**:
same 74 casts and the same 82 columns, but 59,726 rows against 29,863, and its
timestamps carry **seconds** (`14-Oct-2018 18:00:17`) where calcofi.org's are
truncated to the minute (`10/14/2018 18:00`). On that evidence the Shared Drive copy
looks like the *fuller* product, not a stale one.

That matters mostly for `obs_ctd_full` — `ctd_thin` reduces to a ~10 m grid either
way — but `datetime_start_utc` is part of the de-duplication key, so it is not
purely cosmetic. Which copy is authoritative for 2003–2019 is the provider's call,
not this notebook's: see question `calcofi_ctd-cast_20`. Until it is answered the
release keeps what it already had.
:::

```{r}
#| label: pick_archives
#| eval: true

# always evaluates: the chunk above may have set eval=FALSE to skip read+bind when
# resuming from the ctd_raw checkpoint, but `d_zips_read` is also what
# [archive_sources] archives after write_parquet — a resumed render stopped there
# with "object 'd_zips_read' not found" (v2026.11.05). These are data-frame filters
# on the already-listed d_zips, so they cost nothing in either mode.
# a GCS-only final is redundant when calcofi.org already publishes a final for that
# cruise. Everything else — every preliminary, every raw, and every final for a
# cruise calcofi.org has no final for — is read.
cruises_web_final <- d_zips |>
  filter(source == "web", zip_type == "final") |>
  pull(cruise_key) |>
  unique()

d_zips_skip <- d_zips |>
  filter(source == "gcs", zip_type == "final", cruise_key %in% cruises_web_final)

d_zips_read <- d_zips |>
  anti_join(d_zips_skip, by = "file_zip")

d_zips_new_final <- d_zips_read |>
  filter(source == "gcs", zip_type == "final")

say(glue(
  "Archives to read: {nrow(d_zips_read)} of {nrow(d_zips)} ",
  "({nrow(d_zips_skip)} GCS finals skipped as duplicates of calcofi.org; ",
  "{nrow(d_zips_new_final)} GCS finals are new coverage)"))

d_zips_skip |>
  select(file_zip, cruise_key, year, month) |>
  arrange(year, month) |>
  dt(
    caption = glue(
      "Skipped: {nrow(d_zips_skip)} Shared-Drive final archives whose cruise ",
      "calcofi.org already publishes a final for (byte-identical; mirrored to ",
      "GCS but not parsed)"),
    fname = "ctd_zips_skipped"
  )
```

## Download and Unzip Files

```{r}
#| label: download_and_unzip

# `url` is NA for a Shared-Drive-only zip: there is nothing to fetch, the file is
# already in dest_dir (prime_zips_from_gcs put it there). file_zip is passed
# explicitly rather than derived as basename(url), which would be NA for those.
#
# dest_dir (the archive) and ext_dir (its contents) are separate arguments and
# separate filesystems on purpose — see the dir_dl/dir_ext note in [setup].
download_and_unzip <- function(url, file_zip, dest_dir, ext_dir, zip_type,
                               unzip = TRUE) {
  dest_file <- file.path(dest_dir, file_zip)
  dir_unzip <- file.path(ext_dir, str_remove(file_zip, "\\.zip$"))

  if (file_exists(dest_file)) {
    say(glue("Already exists: {file_zip}"))
  } else if (is.na(url)) {
    # primed source vanished between the prime and here — do not silently proceed
    # with a missing archive
    d_dl_fail <<- bind_rows(d_dl_fail, tibble(
      file_zip = file_zip, zip_type = zip_type, url = url, reason = "primed zip missing"))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  } else {
    say(glue("Downloading: {file_zip}"))
    tryCatch(
      download.file(url, dest_file, mode = "wb"),
      error = function(e) {
        # a warning() is invisible in the rendered page and a render with warnings
        # still succeeds: the same nine calcofi.org zips failed this way at every
        # release from August to 2026-10-20. Record it; [download_and_unzip] decides.
        d_dl_fail <<- bind_rows(d_dl_fail, tibble(
          file_zip = file_zip, zip_type = zip_type, url = url, reason = conditionMessage(e)))
        if (file_exists(dest_file)) {
          file_delete(dest_file)
        }
        return(invisible(NULL))
      }
    )
    if (!file_exists(dest_file)) return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  if (!unzip || !zip_type %in% c("final", "preliminary")) {
    if (unzip) say(glue("Skipping unzip (not final/preliminary): {file_zip}"))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # "the directory exists" was the whole completeness test, which reads an
  # INTERRUPTED extraction as a finished one — and the extraction root is now
  # disposable local scratch, so a half-written tree is a routine outcome (a
  # cancelled render, a full disk) rather than a rare one. Compare the file count
  # on disk against the archive's own member count instead. That count comes from
  # the zip's central directory (utils::unzip, NOT the masked `zip::unzip` — see
  # [jrw_overlap_report]), so it costs a seek, not an extraction, per archive.
  # `<`, not `!=`: an archive may legitimately be over-populated (an older run of
  # a since-shrunk archive), and re-extracting on that is churn, not repair.
  # an archive REPLACED under the same name (see above) keeps its member count, so
  # the count below would bless the old extraction: key it on the archive's size and
  # mtime instead, recorded beside the extraction
  stamp_file <- file.path(dir_unzip, ".archive_stamp")
  stamp_now  <- paste(file.size(dest_file), as.numeric(file.mtime(dest_file)))
  stale <- dir_exists(dir_unzip) && if (file_exists(stamp_file))
    !identical(read_lines(stamp_file), stamp_now) else
    file.mtime(dest_file) > file.mtime(dir_unzip)
  if (stale) {
    say(glue("Archive changed since it was extracted — re-extracting {file_zip}"))
    dir_delete(dir_unzip)
  }

  n_members <- sum(!str_detect(utils::unzip(dest_file, list = TRUE)$Name, "/$"))
  n_on_disk <- if (dir_exists(dir_unzip)) {
    length(list.files(dir_unzip, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE,
                      no.. = TRUE))
  } else 0L

  if (n_on_disk >= n_members) {
    say(glue("Already unzipped: {file_zip} ({n_on_disk} files)"))
  } else {
    say(glue(
      "Unzipping: {file_zip} ({n_members} files",
      if (n_on_disk > 0) glue(", {n_on_disk} already present") else "", ")"))
    dir_create(dir_unzip, recurse = TRUE)
    # overwrite = TRUE so a partial extraction is completed rather than skipped
    # around; unzip()'s default leaves an existing (possibly truncated) file be.
    unzip(dest_file, exdir = dir_unzip, overwrite = TRUE)
  }
  write_lines(stamp_now, stamp_file)
}

d_dl_fail <- tibble(file_zip = character(), zip_type = character(),
                    url = character(), reason = character())
d_zips_read |>
  pwalk(function(url, file_zip, zip_type, ...) {
    download_and_unzip(url, file_zip, dir_dl, dir_ext, zip_type, unzip = TRUE)
  })

say(glue("Download and extraction complete: archives in {dir_dl}, ",
         "extracted files in {dir_ext}"))

# a GCS final is skipped above only because calcofi.org publishes a final for the
# same cruise. If that web final then fails to download (calcofi.org lists some
# archives that 404), the cruise has neither copy and vanishes from the release
# without a word: 9501JD, 9712SP and 9803SP-9812SP were missing from every release
# through v2026.10.19 this way. Stop instead.
web_missing <- d_zips_read |>
  filter(source == "web", zip_type %in% c("final", "preliminary"),
         !file_exists(file.path(dir_dl, file_zip)))
lost <- d_zips_skip |> filter(cruise_key %in% web_missing$cruise_key)
if (nrow(lost) > 0)
  stop(glue(
    "calcofi.org final(s) failed to download for {paste(lost$cruise_key, collapse = ', ')}, ",
    "whose Shared Drive final was skipped as their duplicate: read the Shared Drive copy ",
    "(drop the cruise from cruises_web_final) or restore the web archive."))

# every failed archive is shown, and one that leaves its cruise with no final or
# preliminary archive on disk stops the render, unless it is known and has a question
# for the provider: CTD_DL_FAIL_KNOWN maps file_zip to that question's label
CTD_DL_FAIL_KNOWN <- character()
cruises_on_disk <- d_zips_read |>
  filter(zip_type %in% c("final", "preliminary"),
         file_exists(file.path(dir_dl, file_zip))) |>
  pull(cruise_key) |>
  unique()
d_dl_fail <- d_dl_fail |>
  left_join(d_zips_read |> select(file_zip, cruise_key), by = "file_zip") |>
  mutate(cruise_covered = cruise_key %in% cruises_on_disk,
         question       = unname(CTD_DL_FAIL_KNOWN[file_zip]))
if (nrow(d_dl_fail) > 0) {
  dt(d_dl_fail, caption = paste(
    "Archives that failed to download or went missing; a cruise left with no final or",
    "preliminary archive stops the render unless the archive has a provider question"),
    fname = "ctd_zips_failed")
} else say("every archive to read is on disk")
uncovered <- d_dl_fail |>
  filter(zip_type %in% c("final", "preliminary"), !cruise_covered, is.na(question))
if (nrow(uncovered) > 0)
  stop(glue(
    "{nrow(uncovered)} archive(s) failed and left their cruise with no CTD data: ",
    "{paste(uncovered$file_zip, collapse = ', ')}. Restore the file to dir_dl from ",
    "gs://calcofi-files-public/archive/sources/{provider}/{dataset}/, or file a ",
    "provider question and add the file to CTD_DL_FAIL_KNOWN."))

# A provider may re-publish a corrected archive under the same name — the 2607
# preliminary file was, on 2026-09-14, after station numbers >= 100 had shipped cut
# to three digits (CalCOFI/workflows#104). The Shared Drive stays the authoritative
# copy (it primes dir_dl above), so this REPORTS a calcofi.org archive whose size
# differs from the local copy rather than replacing it: replacing it here would swap
# an input without the per-series diff a data fix needs. Only archives this notebook
# reads, only an HTTP 200 (calcofi.org lists some archives that 404), and a failed
# HEAD is simply not reported. Fix a hit by updating the Shared Drive copy.
head_size <- function(url) tryCatch({
  r <- curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = curl::new_handle(
    nobody = TRUE, timeout = 30, followlocation = TRUE))
  if (r$status_code != 200) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(curl::parse_headers_list(r$headers)[["content-length"]] %||% NA)
}, error = function(e) NA_real_)
d_zip_drift <- d_zips_read |>
  filter(!is.na(url), zip_type %in% c("final", "preliminary"),
         file_exists(file.path(dir_dl, file_zip))) |>
  mutate(local_bytes  = file.size(file.path(dir_dl, file_zip)),
         remote_bytes = map_dbl(url, head_size)) |>
  filter(!is.na(remote_bytes), remote_bytes != local_bytes) |>
  select(file_zip, zip_type, local_bytes, remote_bytes, url)
if (nrow(d_zip_drift) > 0) {
  say(glue("{nrow(d_zip_drift)} read archive(s) differ from calcofi.org — update the ",
           "Shared Drive copy and re-render: {paste(d_zip_drift$file_zip, collapse = ', ')}"))
  dt(d_zip_drift, caption = paste(
    "Read archives whose calcofi.org copy differs in size from the local (Shared Drive)",
    "copy: a re-published file the ingest has NOT taken"), fname = "ctd_zip_drift")
} else say("every read archive matches its calcofi.org size (where calcofi.org answers)")
```

### Overlap guard {#jrw-overlap-guard}

Skipping an archive is a claim that nothing is lost by skipping it, so measure the
claim on **every** overlapping cruise rather than trusting one sample. This reads
the zip *directory* (`unzip -l`, no extraction) and compares each top-level
`_CTDBTL_*.csv` against calcofi.org's copy of the same filename by uncompressed
size — a few seconds for all 66, where md5 would mean unpacking ~2 GB.

Size equality is a screen, not a proof; what it reliably catches is the case that
matters, a Shared-Drive copy holding materially more (or less) than the published
one. It does **not** halt the render: a difference here is a question for the
provider, not a defect in this pipeline, and the release keeps what it already had
either way.

```{r}
#| label: jrw_overlap_report

# JRW ships the db CSVs at the archive TOP LEVEL; calcofi.org buries the same
# filenames under db_csv(s)/ inside the _CTDFinalQC archive. Match on basename —
# several cruises split a cruise across separate runs (013-074, 044-060, ...) so
# the file SETS are not always the same shape and a positional compare would lie.
web_btl <- tibble(
  path = list.files(
    dir_ext, pattern = "_CTDBTL_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE,
    recursive = TRUE)) |>
  filter(str_detect(path, "_CTDFinalQC/db[_-]csvs?/")) |>
  mutate(file_csv = basename(path), web_bytes = as.numeric(file_size(path))) |>
  select(file_csv, web_bytes) |>
  distinct(file_csv, .keep_all = TRUE)

# uncompressed sizes straight out of the zip directory — no extraction.
#
# utils::unzip, NOT the bare name: this notebook shelves the `zip` package, whose
# unzip() masks base R's and takes no `list` argument, so `unzip(list = TRUE)`
# fails with "unused argument (list = TRUE)". Everywhere else in this notebook
# unzip() is called only to EXTRACT, where the two signatures happen to agree —
# which is why the masking had never surfaced before.
jrw_btl <- d_zips_skip$file_zip |>
  set_names() |>
  map_dfr(\(fz) {
    z <- utils::unzip(file.path(dir_dl, fz), list = TRUE)
    tibble(file_csv = basename(z$Name), depth = str_count(z$Name, "/"),
           jrw_bytes = z$Length) |>
      filter(str_detect(file_csv, "_CTDBTL_.*\\.csv$"), depth == 0)
  }, .id = "file_zip") |>
  select(-depth)

d_overlap <- jrw_btl |>
  left_join(web_btl, by = "file_csv") |>
  mutate(
    cruise_key = str_extract(file_zip, "\\d{2}-(\\d{4}[A-Z0-9]{2,4})", group = 1),
    ratio  = round(jrw_bytes / web_bytes, 3),
    status = case_when(
      is.na(web_bytes)        ~ "no matching filename on calcofi.org",
      jrw_bytes == web_bytes  ~ "identical size",
      TRUE                    ~ "DIFFERENT size")) |>
  relocate(cruise_key, file_csv, status, ratio, jrw_bytes, web_bytes)

n_same <- sum(d_overlap$status == "identical size")
n_diff <- sum(d_overlap$status == "DIFFERENT size")
n_none <- sum(d_overlap$status == "no matching filename on calcofi.org")

say(glue(
  "Overlap comparison across {n_distinct(d_overlap$cruise_key)} cruises / ",
  "{nrow(d_overlap)} files: {n_same} identical, {n_diff} different, ",
  "{n_none} with no same-named counterpart (split runs)"))

# Not a hard stop — but a WHOLESALE mismatch would mean the wrong folder was
# synced or the layout changed, which is a defect rather than a data question.
stopifnot(
  "no comparable overlap files at all — check the sync and the archive layout" =
    nrow(d_overlap) > 0,
  "the two sources agree on almost nothing — this is a sync/layout problem, not a data question" =
    n_same >= 0.5 * (n_same + n_diff))

d_overlap |>
  filter(status != "identical size") |>
  arrange(desc(ratio)) |>
  dt(
    caption = glue(
      "Shared-Drive vs calcofi.org finals that do NOT match ({n_diff} different ",
      "size, {n_none} split-run). calcofi.org is used for all of these; see ",
      "question calcofi_ctd-cast_20"),
    fname = "ctd_jrw_overlap_diffs"
  )
```

## Find and Prioritize CTD Data Files

CalCOFI's [CTD Cast Files](https://calcofi.org/data/oceanographic-data/ctd-cast-files/)
page names six categories across its header row, three of which are 1 m-binned
products that supersede one another:

**Preliminary CTD 1m-Binned → Preliminary CTD & Bottle 1m-Binned → Final 1m-Binned**

but each cruise offers a **single** `_CTDPrelim.zip`, replaced in place as processing
advances, so the two preliminary tiers are invisible from the zip name. The
discriminator is the CSV filename *inside* the archive — `_CTDBTL_` once the bottle
merge has happened, plain `_CTD_` before it:

| archive | CSV | `data_stage` |
|---|---|---|
| `_CTDFinalQC.zip` (calcofi.org) | `db_csvs/…_CTDBTL_…csv` | `final` |
| `_CTDFinalDB.zip` (Shared Drive) | `…_CTDBTL_…csv` at top level | `final` |
| `_CTDPrelim.zip` | `db-csvs/…_CTDBTL_…csv` | `preliminary_with_bottle` |
| `_CTDPrelim.zip` | `…_CTD_…csv` | `preliminary_without_bottle` |
| `_CTDCast.zip` (Shared Drive, an in-cruise drop) | `…_CTDBTL_…csv` / `…_CTD_…csv` | by its contents, as a `_CTDPrelim.zip` |

A Shared-Drive drop is classified by its **contents**, a calcofi.org link by its name: the
fall 2026 in-cruise drop `20-2611_CTDCast.zip` (Rasmus Swalethorp, 2026-11-04: lines 93.3 and
part of 90, posted from the ship for the media webinar) carries the bottle-merged 1 m-binned
`20-2611_CTDBTL_001-011D.csv` / `…U.csv` under a name the web rule reads as a raw-cast archive,
which is never unzipped. So a local archive whose members are db products
(`_CTD_` / `_CTDBTL_` `NNN-NNN[DU].csv`) is a preliminary drop whatever its name
(`zip_type = "preliminary"` in [d_zips], and the tier arms below key on that, not on
`Prelim` in the folder name); ctd-cast question Q51 asks the provider to confirm the naming.

This matters well beyond labelling. Only the *station-corrected* salinity and oxygen
are canonical — following the provider's own guidance that "station-corrected data
are the best" — and those wait on the bottle merge. A `preliminary_without_bottle`
cruise therefore carries **no corrected salinity or oxygen at all**, which used to
be indistinguishable from a `preliminary_with_bottle` cruise that has them.
Splitting the tier is what lets a consumer tell "not measured" from "not merged
yet".

```{r}
#| label: d_csv

d_csv <- tibble(
  path = list.files(
    dir_ext,
    pattern = "\\.csv$",
    recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    file_csv = basename(path),
    path_unzip = str_replace(path, glue("{dir_ext}/"), ""),
    dir_unzip = str_extract(path_unzip, "^[^/]+")) |>
  # the archive's zip_type from the inventory: a raw-named Shared-Drive drop classified
  # `preliminary` by its contents ([d_zips]) has no `Prelim` in its folder name
  left_join(
    d_zips |> transmute(dir_unzip = str_remove(file_zip, "\\.zip$"), zip_type),
    by = "dir_unzip") |>
  mutate(
    zip_prelim = str_detect(dir_unzip, "Prelim") | coalesce(zip_type == "preliminary", FALSE),
    # ship suffix optional, as in [d_zips]: 20-2611_CTDCast/20-2611_CTDBTL_001-011D.csv
    cruise_key = str_extract(
      path_unzip,
      "\\d{2}-(\\d{4}[A-Z0-9]{0,4})_.*",
      group = 1
    ),
    data_stage = case_when(
      # final, calcofi.org: db_csv(s)/ inside a *Final* archive — EXCEPT the
      # superseded exports some archives keep beside the canonical file:
      # db-csvs/orig/, orig-csvs/, orig_dbcsvs/, uncorrected/. Every cast in those
      # is also in the top-level file (verified over all 16,576 CSVs on disk,
      # 2026-08-24) — except one: 20-0010NH/db-csvs/orig/ carries cast 001, JRW's
      # "First Cast - switch fluorometer" test dip with a 1992 timestamp and scans
      # to 17,178 m, which the canonical file rightly omits. The old unanchored
      # match classified it `final`; casts 002-074 lost to the shorter canonical
      # path in dedup, cast 001 had no competitor, and v2026.08.14 released it at
      # 14,671 m. NOT "top level only": 20-1104SH's db_csvs/separate_runs/ holds
      # casts 031-036 that exist nowhere else, so subfolders that are not
      # superseded exports stay in and dedup picks the canonical copy.
      str_detect(path_unzip, "Final.*db[_|-]csvs?/") &
        !str_detect(path_unzip, regex("db[_|-]csvs?/(orig|uncorrected)[^/]*/",
                                      ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "final",
      # final, Shared Drive: JRW's *_CTDFinalDB archives put the db CSVs at the
      # TOP LEVEL. The top-level restriction is load-bearing — these archives also
      # carry orig/, orig_dbcsvs/, SeparateRuns_Fl/ and south-north/ copies of the
      # same casts. Without it both copies classify `final`, and which one survives
      # falls to the `ORDER BY length("_source_file")` tiebreak in dedup_ctd_raw:
      # correct by accident, and only until a path length changes.
      str_detect(dir_unzip, "CTDFinalDB$") &
        path_unzip == paste0(dir_unzip, "/", file_csv) ~ "final",
      # preliminary, bottle-merged: _CTDBTL_ means the bottle merge has run
      zip_prelim & str_detect(file_csv, "_CTDBTL_") ~ "preliminary_with_bottle",
      # preliminary, sensor only: _CTD_ (no BTL) — corrected salinity/oxygen and
      # every bottle column are empty in these
      zip_prelim & str_detect(file_csv, "_CTD_") ~ "preliminary_without_bottle",
      # NOTE: the hardcoded `cruise_key == "2111SR"` arm that used to sit here is
      # gone, and deliberately. 2111SR puts its db CSVs in csvs-plots/ rather than
      # db-csvs/, so the old *directory*-based rules missed it and it needed a
      # cruise-specific path regex. The rules above key on the FILENAME token and
      # do not care how deep the file sits, so
      # 20-2111SR_CTDPrelim/20-2111SRCTDPrelim/csvs-plots/20-2111SR_CTDBTL_001-075D.csv
      # now classifies as preliminary_with_bottle on its own — which is also
      # accurate than the old arm, which could only say "preliminary". Verified
      # against the archive on disk; a regression would trip the content
      # assertion in [emit_core].
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    # The direction letter is the LAST character of the name — and "last" has to
    # survive a copy marker. Extraction used to land inside Google Drive, which
    # named a conflict copy `19-9501JD_CTDBTL_001-646D 2.csv`; that ends in
    # " 2.csv", matched neither arm of the old `…D\\.csv$` test, and came through
    # as NA. Not cosmetic: [ctd_measurement] joins on cast_dir and NULL = NULL is
    # never true, and [ctd_thin] needs a downcast. Extraction has since moved to
    # `dir_ext`, off Drive, so nothing mints these any more — the stripping stays
    # because it is two regexes against a filename and the archives themselves
    # are not guaranteed free of a name Drive once produced.
    file_stem = file_csv |>
      str_remove("\\.csv$") |>
      str_remove("\\s*\\(\\d+\\)$") |>          # "name (2).csv"
      str_remove("\\s+\\d+$"),                  # "name 2.csv"
    cast_dir = case_when(
      str_detect(file_stem, regex("U$", ignore_case = T)) ~ "U",
      str_detect(file_stem, regex("D$", ignore_case = T)) ~ "D"
    ),
    # supersession order, straight off CTD_DATA_STAGES so a new stage cannot be
    # added to the vocabulary without also being ranked (an unranked stage would
    # otherwise sort last and be silently discarded by the filter below)
    priority = match(data_stage, CTD_DATA_STAGES)
  ) |>
  relocate(cruise_key, path_unzip) |>
  arrange(cruise_key, path_unzip) |>
  filter(data_stage %in% CTD_DATA_STAGES) |>
  # An archive skipped in [pick_archives] is never unzipped — but this chunk globs
  # the extraction directory, not the inventory, so a copy left behind by an
  # earlier run (before the skip existed, or from a run where it was disabled)
  # would still be found here and would compete with calcofi.org's identical copy.
  # Drop them by their unzip directory so the skip decision holds regardless of
  # what is on disk.
  filter(!dir_unzip %in% str_remove(d_zips_skip$file_zip, "\\.zip$"))

# for each cruise keep only the most-advanced stage available:
# final > preliminary_with_bottle > preliminary_without_bottle
d_priority <- d_csv |>
  group_by(cruise_key) |>
  summarize(
    best_priority = min(priority),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

d_csv <- d_csv |>
  inner_join(d_priority, by = "cruise_key") |>
  filter(priority == best_priority) |>
  select(-best_priority)

# A file whose name does not END in a direction letter is not a db product this
# ingest reads. Four exist — `…084IDnoQC.csv` and `…067Dno001b.csv` pairs — and
# they sit beside the canonical D/U pair inside the same archive. Carrying them
# with `cast_dir = NA` was strictly worse than dropping them: [ctd_measurement]
# joins on cast_dir, `NULL = NULL` is never true, so they became 112,245 cast
# rows that could hold no measurement and still reached `sample` as casts with
# nothing under them. Drop them, and say which.
d_csv_nodir <- d_csv |> filter(is.na(cast_dir))
d_csv       <- d_csv |> filter(!is.na(cast_dir))

if (nrow(d_csv_nodir) > 0)
  d_csv_nodir |>
    select(cruise_key, file_csv, data_stage) |>
    arrange(cruise_key, file_csv) |>
    dt(
      caption = glue(
        "Skipped: {nrow(d_csv_nodir)} file(s) whose name resolves no cast ",
        "direction (alternate renderings beside the canonical D/U pair)"),
      fname = "ctd_files_no_cast_direction")

# --- one copy of each file: an archive holding two is resolved here, once ----------
# Eight preliminary archives carry the same db file twice, under two folders
# (db-csvs/ + csvs-plots/ or db-csvs/ + metadata/). Seven pairs are byte-identical,
# so reading both cost nothing but time: [dedup_ctd_raw] collapsed every row. The
# 2204SH pair is NOT identical (CalCOFI/workflows#131): db-csvs/ is the May 2022
# export, csvs-plots/ the February 2025 re-export, which adds nutrients (NO3, NO2,
# NH4, PO4, SIL), BTL_Temp and 559 more OxBuM bottles, corrects Ox*uM_StaCorr (the
# May 2022 copy holds ~57-81 µmol/kg at the surface beside ~282 from the cruise
# correction) and re-derives Ox*_StaCorr / EstChl_StaCorr; it also writes times to
# the minute and SPAR/PAR to three significant figures, no longer carries 7
# shallow bottles (casts 007d, 008d, 079d, 100d) and moves one (040d, 101 -> 102 m).
# Because the two copies write the time differently, dedup's key never matched:
# v2026.10.01 shipped both, 2,941,303 duplicated (cast, depth, type) keys in obs +
# obs_ctd_full. Where a May 2022 scan fell on a whole minute (hh:mm:00) its key DID
# match the re-export's minute, and the shorter db-csvs/ path won dedup's tiebreak:
# 14 bottles lost their nutrients, BTL_Temp and (8 of them) OxBuM, the 92 values
# #131 found missing.
#
# So a cruise is read from ONE copy, chosen before any row is read: byte-identical
# copies keep the shortest path (what dedup picked anyway, so no value changes);
# differing copies keep the folder declared below and stop the render when none
# is declared, because which export is current is a fact about the provider's
# processing, not something a path length can decide.
CTD_COPY_PREFER <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cruise_key, ~keep_folder,  ~reason,
  "2204SH",    "csvs-plots", paste(
    "February 2025 re-export: nutrients, BTL_Temp, corrected Ox*uM_StaCorr;",
    "the May 2022 db-csvs/ copy has neither (CalCOFI/workflows#131)"))

d_csv_copies <- d_csv |>
  group_by(cruise_key, dir_unzip, file_stem) |>
  filter(n() > 1) |>
  mutate(
    md5        = unname(tools::md5sum(path)),
    identical  = n_distinct(md5) == 1,
    folder     = str_extract(path_unzip, "[^/]+(?=/[^/]+$)")) |>
  left_join(CTD_COPY_PREFER, by = "cruise_key") |>
  mutate(
    keep = if_else(
      identical,
      row_number(paste(str_pad(nchar(path_unzip), 4, pad = "0"), path_unzip)) == 1,
      !is.na(keep_folder) & folder == keep_folder)) |>
  ungroup()

copies_undeclared <- d_csv_copies |>
  group_by(cruise_key, dir_unzip, file_stem) |>
  filter(sum(keep) != 1) |>
  ungroup()
if (nrow(copies_undeclared) > 0)
  stop(glue(
    "an archive holds differing copies of the same CTD file and CTD_COPY_PREFER ",
    "names no single one to read: ",
    paste(unique(copies_undeclared$path_unzip), collapse = "; "),
    ". Decide which export is current (compare the columns) and declare it."))

if (nrow(d_csv_copies) > 0) {
  say(glue(
    "one copy per file: {sum(!d_csv_copies$keep)} duplicate file(s) not read in ",
    "{n_distinct(d_csv_copies$cruise_key)} cruise(s) ",
    "({sum(!d_csv_copies$keep & !d_csv_copies$identical)} differing: ",
    "{paste(unique(d_csv_copies$cruise_key[!d_csv_copies$identical]), collapse = ', ')})"))
  d_csv_copies |>
    transmute(cruise_key, path_unzip, identical, read = keep,
              reason = if_else(identical, "byte-identical copy: shortest path read", reason)) |>
    arrange(cruise_key, path_unzip) |>
    dt(caption = paste(
      "Archives holding the same CTD file twice: the copy read, the copy skipped",
      "(differing copies resolved by CTD_COPY_PREFER)"),
      fname = "ctd_files_copies_resolved")
  d_csv <- d_csv |>
    filter(!path_unzip %in% d_csv_copies$path_unzip[!d_csv_copies$keep])
}
stopifnot(
  "one file per (cruise, archive, file stem) after resolving copies" =
    !any(duplicated(d_csv[c("cruise_key", "dir_unzip", "file_stem")])))

# Every cruise must keep a downcast. [ctd_thin] takes one direction per physical
# cast and prefers D, so a cruise with no D produces no thin rows and therefore
# no `obs` — and because write_parquet_outputs() DELETES a partition that has
# left the data, and sync_to_gcs() mirrors the deletion, the cruise then leaves
# the release entirely while its casts survive in `sample`. That is precisely how
# v2026.08.08 lost 10 cruises and 874,000 observations with no error anywhere.
cruises_no_downcast <- d_csv |>
  group_by(cruise_key) |>
  summarize(has_downcast = any(cast_dir == "D"), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(!has_downcast) |>
  pull(cruise_key)

if (length(cruises_no_downcast) > 0)
  stop(glue(
    "{length(cruises_no_downcast)} cruise(s) have no downcast file: ",
    "{paste(cruises_no_downcast, collapse = ', ')}.\n",
    "ctd_thin cannot emit a headline profile for them, so they would reach the ",
    "release as casts with no observations."))

cruises_csv_notzip <- setdiff(
  unique(d_csv$cruise_key),
  unique(d_zips$cruise_key)
) |>
  sort()
stopifnot(length(cruises_csv_notzip) == 0)

cruises_zip_notcsv <- setdiff(
  unique(d_zips$cruise_key),
  unique(d_csv$cruise_key)
) |>
  sort()

d_csv |>
  select(-any_of(c("path", "data", "col_empties", "col_types"))) |>
  relocate(cruise_key, path_unzip) |>
  arrange(cruise_key, path_unzip) |>
  dt(
    caption = "Files to Ingest",
    fname = "ctd_files_to_ingest"
  )
```

## Read and Standardize CTD Files

Remove repeat header rows that can occur within files.

```{r}
#| label: read_csv

d_csv <- d_csv |>
  arrange(basename(path)) |>
  mutate(
    data = map2(path, seq_along(path), \(path, idx) {
      say(glue("Reading {idx}/{nrow(d_csv)}: {basename(path)}"))

      all_lines <- read_lines(path)
      header_line <- all_lines[1]

      # find repeat header rows (excluding row 1)
      repeat_header_rows <- which(all_lines[-1] == header_line)

      if (length(repeat_header_rows) > 0) {
        all_lines <- all_lines[-(repeat_header_rows + 1)]
        tmp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
        write_lines(all_lines, tmp_file)
        data <- read_csv(tmp_file, guess_max = Inf, show_col_types = F) |>
          clean_names()
        file_delete(tmp_file)
      } else {
        data <- read_csv(path, guess_max = Inf, show_col_types = F) |>
          clean_names()
      }
      # a flag column the provider left empty throughout a file reads as logical
      # (all NA). Make every flag column numeric so the files bind to one type and
      # COALESCE(provider flag, sensor flag) below never mixes BOOLEAN with DOUBLE.
      #
      # ...and DROP a 2026-layout flag column the file leaves wholly empty. bind_rows
      # broadcasts every column to every scan of the archive, so the 27 new *Q columns
      # of ONE file (the corrected 2607 preliminary, every code empty) became ~30M
      # doubles each and took R past its 24 GB vector limit in
      # [pts_distance_from_lnst] (run of 2026-09-23). An all-empty column carries no
      # flag, and [meas_col_registry] adds any flag column still missing as NULL
      # before the COALESCE, so dropping it loses nothing.
      q_new <- c("temp_ave_q", "salt1_corr_q", "salt2_corr_q", "salt_ave_corr_q",
                 "ox1_cruise_corr_q", "ox1_sta_corr_q", "ox2_cruise_corr_q",
                 "ox2_sta_corr_q", "ox_ave_sta_corr_q", "ox1u_mq", "ox1u_m_cruise_corr_q",
                 "ox1u_m_sta_corr_q", "ox2u_mq", "ox2u_m_cruise_corr_q", "ox2u_m_sta_corr_q",
                 "ox_aveu_m_sta_corr_q", "est_chl_cruise_corr_q", "est_chl_sta_corr_q",
                 "est_no3_cruise_corr_q", "est_no3_sta_corr_q", "batq", "po_t1q", "po_t2q",
                 "dyn_ht_q", "svaq", "ox_sat1q", "ox_sat2q")
      q_empty <- intersect(q_new, names(data))[
        vapply(intersect(q_new, names(data)), \(c) all(is.na(data[[c]])), logical(1))]
      data |>
        mutate(across(where(is.logical) & matches("q$"), as.numeric)) |>
        # the layout marker survives the drop (the cross-check needs it)
        mutate(.src_qc_2026 = "salt_ave_corr_q" %in% names(data)) |>
        select(-any_of(q_empty))
    }),
    nrows = map_int(data, ~ if (is.null(.x)) 0 else nrow(.x)),
    # the file layout: the CTD team's 2026 processing software writes a quality
    # code for every corrected, averaged and derived series (SaltAve_CorrQ,
    # OxAve_StaCorrQ, EstChl_StaCorrQ, …; CalCOFI/workflows#105), the legacy
    # layout flags only the sensors. The cross-check in [combine_sensor_pairs]
    # reads it.
    src_format = map_chr(data, ~ if (isTRUE(.x$.src_qc_2026[1])) "qc_2026" else "legacy"),
    data = map(data, ~ select(.x, -.src_qc_2026))
  )

say(glue("file layouts: {paste(names(table(d_csv$src_format)), table(d_csv$src_format), sep = ' = ', collapse = ', ')}"))
write_rds(d_csv |> transmute(`_source_file` = path_unzip, src_format),
          glue("{dir_tmp}/d_src_format.rds"))

d_csv |>
  arrange(cruise_key, file_csv) |>
  select(cruise_key, file_csv, nrows, src_format) |>
  dt(
    caption = "Number of rows read per file",
    fname = "ctd_rows_per_file"
  ) |>
  formatCurrency("nrows", currency = "", digits = 0, mark = ",")

# A file that reads zero rows is a failure, not an observation — and it is the
# one failure this pipeline could not see.
#
# Extraction used to land inside Google Drive, which evicts a synced file to a
# cloud-only placeholder. `list.files()` still reported the full size (12,254,953
# bytes for 19-9501JD_CTDBTL_001-646D.csv) and `ls -lO` marked it `dataless`, but
# reading it timed out at the filesystem and `read_csv()` returned a **0-row
# tibble with no error**. On the v2026.08.08 run 20 files across 14 cruises read 0
# rows exactly this way. Nothing downstream distinguishes "this cruise has no
# downcast" from "the downcast file was empty".
#
# `dir_ext` is now plain local disk, so that specific cause is gone — but the
# assertion stays, because what it really tests is that the bytes reaching the
# pivot are the bytes in the archive, and a truncated extraction says the same
# thing. The remedy just changed: delete the archive's extraction directory and
# re-render, rather than coaxing a file back out of Drive.
d_csv_empty <- d_csv |> filter(nrows == 0)

if (nrow(d_csv_empty) > 0)
  stop(glue(
    "{nrow(d_csv_empty)} CSV(s) read 0 rows:\n",
    paste0("  ", d_csv_empty$path_unzip, collapse = "\n"), "\n",
    "A CTD db CSV is never legitimately empty — its extraction is incomplete. ",
    "Delete the offending director(ies) under {dir_ext} and re-render; ",
    "[download_and_unzip] re-extracts from the archive in {dir_dl}."))
```

## Detect and Correct Column Type Mismatches

```{r}
#| label: d_bind

d_csv <- d_csv |>
  mutate(
    col_empties = map(data, \(x) {
      tibble(
        col_name = names(x),
        n_empty = map_int(x, \(col) sum(is.na(col)))
      ) |>
        filter(n_empty == nrow(x)) |>
        pull(col_name)
    }),
    col_types = map2(data, col_empties, \(x, y) {
      tibble(
        col_name = names(x),
        col_type = map_chr(x, \(col) class(col)[1])
      ) |>
        filter(!col_name %in% y)
    })
  )

# find most common type for each column across all files
d_types <- d_csv |>
  select(path, col_types) |>
  unnest(col_types) |>
  count(col_name, col_type) |>
  group_by(col_name) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(col_name, expected_type = col_type)

d_mismatches <- d_csv |>
  select(cruise_key, path, col_types) |>
  unnest(col_types) |>
  left_join(d_types, by = "col_name") |>
  filter(col_type != expected_type) |>
  arrange(col_name, path)

if (nrow(d_mismatches) > 0) {
  say("Type mismatches detected - converting columns...")
}

# bind data, converting mismatched columns to expected type
d_bind <- d_csv |>
  mutate(
    data = map2(data, path, \(x, p) {
      x_mismatches <- d_mismatches |>
        filter(path == p)

      if (nrow(x_mismatches) > 0) {
        for (i in 1:nrow(x_mismatches)) {
          col <- x_mismatches$col_name[i]
          expected <- x_mismatches$expected_type[i]
          na_before <- sum(is.na(x[[col]]))

          suppressWarnings({
            x[[col]] <- switch(
              expected,
              "numeric" = as.numeric(x[[col]]),
              "integer" = as.integer(x[[col]]),
              "logical" = as.logical(x[[col]]),
              "character" = as.character(x[[col]]),
              x[[col]]
            )
          })

          na_after <- sum(is.na(x[[col]]))
          na_generated <- na_after - na_before

          if (na_generated > 0) {
            say(glue(
              "  {basename(p)}: {col} ({x_mismatches$col_type[i]} -> {expected}) generated {na_generated} NAs"
            ))
          }

          d_mismatches[
            d_mismatches$path == p & d_mismatches$col_name == col,
            "nas_generated"
          ] <<- na_generated
        }
      }
      x
    })
  ) |>
  unnest(data)

if (nrow(d_mismatches) > 0) {
  d_mismatches |>
    group_by(col_name, expected_type, col_type) |>
    summarize(
      n_files = n(),
      total_nas = sum(nas_generated, na.rm = TRUE),
      files = paste(basename(path), collapse = "; "),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(total_nas)) |>
    dt(
      caption = "Type mismatches by column",
      fname = "ctd_type_mismatches_by_column"
    ) |>
    formatCurrency(
      c("n_files", "total_nas"),
      currency = "",
      digits = 0,
      mark = ","
    )
}

# reconcile cruise_key from study where mismatched
d_bind <- d_bind |>
  mutate(
    cruise_key = if_else(
      !is.na(study) &
        cruise_key != study &
        study != "Study",
      study,
      cruise_key
    ),
    `_source_file` = path_unzip
  ) |>
  relocate(`_source_file`, .after = cruise_key) |>
  select(
    -path_unzip,
    -path,
    -file_csv,
    -dir_unzip,
    -priority,
    -project,
    -study,
    -nrows,
    -col_empties,
    -col_types,
    -src_format
  )

# fill missing ord_occ from cast_id
d_bind <- d_bind |>
  mutate(
    ord_occ = if_else(
      is.na(ord_occ) & !is.na(cast_id),
      str_extract(cast_id, "_(\\d{3})", group = 1),
      ord_occ
    )
  )

# --- a cast's direction is its Cast_ID's, not its file's ---------------------
# The downcast files of 1604SH and 2105SH carry seven UPcasts (1604_003u, _034u,
# _042u, _082u, _099u; 2105_019u, _043u: 1,756 rows), each the only cast of its
# occupation and each byte-for-byte the same rows as in the U file. Tagged with the
# file's direction they kept a `cast_dir` of D, so [dedup_ctd_raw] (which keys on
# cast_dir) never matched them to their U-file twins and every one reached obs and
# obs_ctd_full twice under the same sample_key (CalCOFI/workflows#131 item 5:
# 75,310 duplicated keys in v2026.10.01). Take the direction from the Cast_ID's last letter; drop
# a mis-filed row whose twin sits in the file of its own direction, and re-tag one
# that has no twin so nothing is lost.
id_dir <- toupper(str_extract(d_bind$cast_id, "[dDuU]$"))
i_misdir <- which(!is.na(id_dir) & id_dir != d_bind$cast_dir)
if (length(i_misdir) > 0) {
  d_misdir <- d_bind[i_misdir, c("cruise_key", "_source_file", "cast_id", "depth", "date_time_utc")]
  # only the rows of the same casts: the whole frame is ~30M scans
  i_same   <- setdiff(which(d_bind$cast_id %in% unique(d_misdir$cast_id)), i_misdir)
  ok_dir   <- d_bind[i_same, c("cruise_key", "cast_id", "depth", "date_time_utc")]
  has_twin <- vctrs::vec_in(d_misdir[c("cruise_key", "cast_id", "depth", "date_time_utc")], ok_dir)
  d_misdir |>
    mutate(twin = has_twin) |>
    group_by(cruise_key, file = basename(`_source_file`), cast_id) |>
    summarize(n_rows = n(), n_dropped_twin = sum(twin), n_retagged = sum(!twin),
              .groups = "drop") |>
    dt(caption = paste(
      "Casts filed under the wrong direction: a row whose twin is in the file of its",
      "Cast_ID's direction is dropped, one without a twin takes that direction"),
      fname = "ctd_casts_wrong_direction_file")
  say(glue("casts filed under the wrong direction: {n_distinct(d_misdir$cast_id)} casts, ",
           "{sum(has_twin)} rows dropped as twins, {sum(!has_twin)} re-tagged"))
  d_bind$cast_dir[i_misdir[!has_twin]] <- id_dir[i_misdir[!has_twin]]
  if (any(has_twin)) d_bind <- d_bind[-i_misdir[has_twin], ]
  rm(d_misdir, ok_dir, has_twin, i_same)
}
rm(id_dir, i_misdir)

# normalize raw coordinate column names (CalCOFI CTD CSV ships Lon_Dec/Lat_Dec ->
# clean_names lon_dec/lat_dec) to the canonical dictionary names used downstream
d_bind <- d_bind |>
  rename(longitude = lon_dec, latitude = lat_dec)

# save intermediate for resumability
write_rds(d_bind, glue("{dir_tmp}/d_bind_pre_datetime.rds"), compress = "gz")
```

## Format Date-Time Column

```{r}
#| label: format_datetime

d_bind <- read_rds(glue("{dir_tmp}/d_bind_pre_datetime.rds"))

d_bind <- d_bind |>
  mutate(
    date_time_utc = trimws(date_time_utc),
    date_time_format = case_when(
      str_detect(
        date_time_utc,
        "^\\d{1,2}-[A-z]{3}-\\d{4} \\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}$"
      ) ~ "dmy_hms",
      str_detect(
        date_time_utc,
        "^\\d{1,2}/\\d{1,2}/\\d{4} \\d{1,2}:\\d{1,2}$"
      ) ~ "mdy_hm",
      TRUE ~ "unknown"
    ),
    datetime_start_utc = NA,
    datetime_start_utc = if_else(
      date_time_format == "dmy_hms",
      suppressWarnings(dmy_hms(date_time_utc, tz = "UTC")),
      datetime_start_utc
    ),
    datetime_start_utc = if_else(
      date_time_format == "mdy_hm",
      suppressWarnings(mdy_hm(date_time_utc, tz = "UTC")),
      datetime_start_utc
    )
  ) |>
  relocate(date_time_format, datetime_start_utc, .after = date_time_utc) |>
  arrange(datetime_start_utc, depth)

stopifnot(all(!is.na(d_bind$datetime_start_utc)))

write_rds(d_bind, glue("{dir_tmp}/d_bind_post_datetime.rds"), compress = "gz")

d_bind |>
  group_by(cruise_key, `_source_file`, date_time_format) |>
  summarize(
    n_records = n(),
    datetime_min = min(datetime_start_utc),
    datetime_max = max(datetime_start_utc),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(cruise_key, `_source_file`, date_time_format) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = date_time_format,
    values_from = n_records,
    values_fill = NA_real_
  ) |>
  relocate(dmy_hms, mdy_hm, .after = cruise_key) |>
  dt(
    caption = "Date-Time formats detected by cruise_key and source_file",
    fname = "ctd_datetime_formats"
  ) |>
  formatDate(c("datetime_min", "datetime_max"), method = "toLocaleString")
```

## Pseudo-NA Values and Fill Missing Coordinates

```{r}
#| label: fill_lonlat

d_bind <- read_rds(glue("{dir_tmp}/d_bind_post_datetime.rds"))

pseudoNA_values <- c(-9.99e-29, -99)

# --- station numbers cut to three digits: repaired by the cast's own position ---
# The CTD team's preliminary files for 2507SR, 2511SR, 2601RL, 2604SH and 2607SH
# wrote station numbers >= 100 with three digits: 100/110/120 read as 000/010/020
# (`Sta` "000.0", `Sta_ID` "090.0 000.0"). The distance filter then dropped every
# such cast as a position error, so those cruises lost their offshore stations in
# every release through v2026.09.11 (CalCOFI/workflows#104). The provider re-issued
# 2607 on 2026-09-14, and the ONLY difference is `Sta`/`Sta_ID` = station + 100; the
# other four are not re-issued yet (questions.csv Q39). So repair exactly that, and
# only where the cast's recorded GPS position says so: an inshore number (< 30)
# whose cast lies within CTD_TRUNC_KM of station + 100 and farther than that from
# the station as written. Every repair is listed below; [filter_pts] still stops the
# render if a truncated station survives unrepaired.
CTD_TRUNC_KM <- 10   # the distance filter's own cutoff (max_dist_dec_lnst_km)
sta_num  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d_bind$sta))
line_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d_bind$line))
i_cand <- which(!is.na(sta_num) & !is.na(line_num) & sta_num < 30 & line_num > 0 &
                  !is.na(d_bind$longitude) & !is.na(d_bind$latitude) &
                  d_bind$longitude > -180 & d_bind$latitude > -90)
d_trunc_fix <- tibble(
  .i = i_cand, src = d_bind$`_source_file`[i_cand], cast_id = d_bind$cast_id[i_cand],
  line = line_num[i_cand], sta = sta_num[i_cand],
  lon = d_bind$longitude[i_cand], lat = d_bind$latitude[i_cand]) |>
  group_by(src, cast_id, line, sta) |>
  summarize(lon = median(lon), lat = median(lat), n_scans = n(), .groups = "drop")
if (nrow(d_trunc_fix) > 0) {
  nominal <- function(line, sta) sf_project(
    from = "+proj=calcofi", to = "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84", pts = cbind(line, sta))
  hav_km <- function(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2) {
    r <- pi / 180
    a <- sin((lat2 - lat1) * r / 2)^2 +
      cos(lat1 * r) * cos(lat2 * r) * sin((lon2 - lon1) * r / 2)^2
    2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(a))
  }
  xy0   <- nominal(d_trunc_fix$line, d_trunc_fix$sta)
  xy100 <- nominal(d_trunc_fix$line, d_trunc_fix$sta + 100)
  d_trunc_fix <- d_trunc_fix |>
    mutate(km_as_written = hav_km(lon, lat, xy0[, 1], xy0[, 2]),
           km_plus_100   = hav_km(lon, lat, xy100[, 1], xy100[, 2])) |>
    filter(km_plus_100 <= CTD_TRUNC_KM, km_as_written > CTD_TRUNC_KM)
}
if (nrow(d_trunc_fix) > 0) {
  key_fix <- paste(d_trunc_fix$src, d_trunc_fix$cast_id, d_trunc_fix$line, d_trunc_fix$sta)
  i_fix   <- i_cand[paste(d_bind$`_source_file`[i_cand], d_bind$cast_id[i_cand],
                          line_num[i_cand], sta_num[i_cand]) %in% key_fix]
  sta_new <- sta_num[i_fix] + 100
  d_bind$sta[i_fix] <- if (is.character(d_bind$sta)) sprintf("%05.1f", sta_new) else sta_new
  d_bind$sta_id[i_fix] <- sprintf("%05.1f %05.1f", line_num[i_fix], sta_new)
  say(glue("station numbers repaired (+100, confirmed by position): ",
           "{nrow(d_trunc_fix)} casts, {format(length(i_fix), big.mark = ',')} scans, ",
           "files: {paste(unique(basename(d_trunc_fix$src)), collapse = ', ')}"))
  write_rds(d_trunc_fix, glue("{dir_tmp}/d_station_truncation_repaired.rds"))
  d_trunc_fix |>
    mutate(file = basename(src), sta_repaired = sta + 100) |>
    select(file, cast_id, line, sta_as_written = sta, sta_repaired, n_scans,
           km_as_written, km_plus_100) |>
    dt(caption = paste(
      "Station numbers cut to three digits by the source, repaired to station + 100",
      "where the cast's recorded position confirms it (CalCOFI/workflows#104)"),
      fname = "ctd_station_truncation_repaired")
} else say("no truncated station numbers found")
rm(sta_num, line_num, i_cand)

# --- a line number the provider wrote wrong: an explicit override per cast ------
# 2204SH casts 094 and 095 (both directions) write `Sta_ID` 066.3 070.0 / 066.3 060.0,
# but the ship sat 0.6 km and 0.2 km from 063.3 070.0 / 063.3 060.0 and 66 km from the
# stations as written, between casts 093 (063.3 080.0) and 096 (063.3 055.0) of the same
# line. The distance filter dropped both casts whole (199 bottle values; CalCOFI/
# workflows#131 item 2). Unlike the truncation above this is not a pattern to detect, so
# it is keyed on cruise + cast and still confirmed by the cast's own median position: an
# override whose position no longer agrees stops the render, and one that matches no
# scan (the provider re-issued the file) is reported and does nothing. The question to
# the provider stays open (questions.csv Q43).
CTD_STATION_OVERRIDE <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cruise_key, ~cast_base,  ~line_as_written, ~line_repaired, ~question,
  "2204SH",    "2204_094",  66.3,             63.3,           "calcofi_ctd-cast_43",
  "2204SH",    "2204_095",  66.3,             63.3,           "calcofi_ctd-cast_43")
cast_base_all <- str_remove(d_bind$cast_id, "[dDuU]$")
d_sta_fix <- purrr::pmap_dfr(CTD_STATION_OVERRIDE, function(cruise_key, cast_base, line_as_written,
                                                            line_repaired, question) {
  i <- which(d_bind$cruise_key == cruise_key & cast_base_all == cast_base &
               abs(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d_bind$line)) - line_as_written) < 1e-6)
  if (!length(i)) return(tibble(cruise_key, cast_base, n_scans = 0L))
  sta <- unique(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d_bind$sta[i])))
  ok  <- d_bind$longitude[i] > -180 & d_bind$latitude[i] > -90
  lon <- median(d_bind$longitude[i][ok]); lat <- median(d_bind$latitude[i][ok])
  xy_w <- sf_project(from = "+proj=calcofi", to = "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84",
                     pts = cbind(line_as_written, sta))
  xy_r <- sf_project(from = "+proj=calcofi", to = "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84",
                     pts = cbind(line_repaired, sta))
  r <- pi / 180
  km <- function(x, y) 2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(sin((y - lat) * r / 2)^2 +
    cos(lat * r) * cos(y * r) * sin((x - lon) * r / 2)^2))
  km_written <- km(xy_w[, 1], xy_w[, 2]); km_repaired <- km(xy_r[, 1], xy_r[, 2])
  if (length(sta) != 1 || !(km_repaired <= CTD_TRUNC_KM && km_written > CTD_TRUNC_KM))
    stop(glue("station override {cruise_key} {cast_base}: the cast's median position does ",
              "not confirm line {line_repaired} (km as written {round(km_written, 1)}, ",
              "repaired {round(km_repaired, 1)}). Re-check the source before overriding."))
  d_bind$line[i]   <<- if (is.character(d_bind$line)) sprintf("%05.1f", line_repaired) else line_repaired
  d_bind$sta_id[i] <<- sprintf("%05.1f %05.1f", line_repaired, sta)
  tibble(cruise_key, cast_base, line_as_written, line_repaired, sta, n_scans = length(i),
         km_as_written = km_written, km_repaired = km_repaired, question)
})
rm(cast_base_all)
if (sum(d_sta_fix$n_scans) > 0) {
  say(glue("line numbers repaired by override: {sum(d_sta_fix$n_scans > 0)} cast(s), ",
           "{format(sum(d_sta_fix$n_scans), big.mark = ',')} scans"))
  dt(d_sta_fix, caption = paste(
    "Line numbers the source wrote wrong, repaired per cast where the cast's median",
    "position confirms the repair (CTD_STATION_OVERRIDE; CalCOFI/workflows#131)"),
    fname = "ctd_station_override_repaired")
}
if (any(d_sta_fix$n_scans == 0))
  say(glue("station override matched no scan (source re-issued?): ",
           "{paste(d_sta_fix$cast_base[d_sta_fix$n_scans == 0], collapse = ', ')}"))

d_bind <- d_bind |>
  mutate(
    is_lnsta_pseudoNA = ifelse(
      as.numeric(line) == 0 & as.numeric(sta) == 0,
      TRUE,
      FALSE
    ),
    is_lon_pseudoNA = map_lgl(longitude, ~ some(pseudoNA_values, near, .x)),
    is_lat_pseudoNA = map_lgl(latitude, ~ some(pseudoNA_values, near, .x)),
    longitude = if_else(
      is_lon_pseudoNA | is_lat_pseudoNA,
      NA_real_,
      longitude
    ),
    latitude = if_else(
      is_lon_pseudoNA | is_lat_pseudoNA,
      NA_real_,
      latitude
    ),
    lon_lnst = if_else(
      !is.na(line) & !is.na(sta) & !is_lnsta_pseudoNA,
      as.numeric(sf_project(
        from = "+proj=calcofi",
        to = "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84",
        pts = cbind(x = as.numeric(line), y = as.numeric(sta))
      )[, 1]),
      NA_real_
    ),
    lat_lnst = if_else(
      !is.na(line) & !is.na(sta) & !is_lnsta_pseudoNA,
      as.numeric(sf_project(
        from = "+proj=calcofi",
        to = "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84",
        pts = cbind(x = as.numeric(line), y = as.numeric(sta))
      )[, 2]),
      NA_real_
    ),
    longitude = if_else(is.na(longitude), lon_lnst, longitude),
    latitude = if_else(is.na(latitude), lat_lnst, latitude)
  )

# A scan with no position AND no CalCOFI line/station to derive one from cannot
# be placed, so it cannot enter `sample`/`obs` (both key on a position). Until
# 2026-08-24 this was a bare hard stop, which held for years because every such
# scan had a line/station. Then calcofi.org's 19-9604JD and 19-9608NH FinalQC
# archives (fetched for the first time that day; JRW's FinalDB copies omit them)
# brought 9,225 scans from the "RATHBURN CORE STN" canyon site: lat/lon -99 and
# the station NAME in the line/sta columns. Those are not CalCOFI grid casts
# (questions.csv Q, "Rathburn"). Report them by file and drop them; the assertion
# below still holds for everything placeable, and the drop is bounded so an
# archive that loses its positions wholesale fails loudly rather than vanishing.
CTD_UNPLACED_MAX_PCT <- 0.2   # 9,225 of 9,135,263 = 0.10% at 2026-08-24; only ever DOWN

d_unplaced <- d_bind |>
  filter(is.na(longitude) | is.na(latitude))
if (nrow(d_unplaced) > 0) {
  d_unplaced |>
    count(cruise_key, `_source_file`, line, sta, name = "n_scans") |>
    arrange(desc(n_scans)) |>
    dt(
      caption = glue(
        "{format(nrow(d_unplaced), big.mark = ',')} scans DROPPED: no position and ",
        "no line/station to derive one from"),
      fname = "ctd_scans_unplaced")
}
stopifnot(
  "unplaceable scans exceed the ratchet: a source lost its positions; investigate before dropping" =
    100 * nrow(d_unplaced) / nrow(d_bind) <= CTD_UNPLACED_MAX_PCT)
d_bind <- d_bind |>
  filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude))

stopifnot(sum(is.na(d_bind$longitude)) == 0)
stopifnot(sum(is.na(d_bind$latitude)) == 0)

# --- a cast is on station as a whole: its MEDIAN position decides --------------
# Until #131 the distance filter tested every scan, so a scan whose GPS fix glitched
# (2404SH: 674 scans on 143 casts, lat 226 or lon -245 in the middle of an otherwise
# steady cast; 626 of them beyond 10 km) was dropped with its measurements, 11 bottles
# among them, and a cast was kept piecewise; the 48 within 10 km were published at
# the glitched position. Now the cast's median position is tested: a cast
# within CTD_TRUNC_KM (the filter's 10 km) of its station keeps EVERY scan, and a
# scan more than CTD_GLITCH_DEG from that median keeps its measurements and takes
# the cast's median position. A cast whose median fails (truly off station, or a GPS
# feed corrupt on most scans, as on several 0310NH / 0711NH casts) falls back to the
# per-scan test in [filter_pts], so it keeps exactly what it kept before.
#
# CTD_OFF_STATION_KEEP: a real occupation off its station is not a position error.
# 2504SH cast 045 (both directions) sits 11.0 km from nominal 083.3 039.4 on a steady
# GPS track (scans within 0.05 km of each other); GEBCO gives 45 m at the recorded
# position and 24 m at the nominal one, and the cast reached 32 m, so it cannot have
# been at the nominal position. It keeps its true position and its nominal station
# (site_key 083.3 039.4); the distance is listed in the table below.
CTD_GLITCH_DEG <- 0.05
CTD_OFF_STATION_KEEP <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cruise_key, ~cast_base, ~max_km, ~reason,
  "2504SH",    "2504_045", 12,      paste(
    "11.0 km off 083.3 039.4 on a steady GPS track; 32 m cast where GEBCO is 24 m at",
    "the nominal position and 45 m at the recorded one (CalCOFI/workflows#131)"))

cast_gid <- as.integer(vctrs::vec_group_id(d_bind[c("_source_file", "cast_id", "line", "sta")]))
d_cast_pos <- tibble(gid = cast_gid, lon = d_bind$longitude, lat = d_bind$latitude,
                     lon_lnst = d_bind$lon_lnst, lat_lnst = d_bind$lat_lnst) |>
  group_by(gid) |>
  summarize(lon_med = median(lon), lat_med = median(lat),
            lon_lnst = first(lon_lnst), lat_lnst = first(lat_lnst), n_scans = n(),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(gid)
stopifnot("cast groups numbered 1..n" = all(d_cast_pos$gid == seq_len(nrow(d_cast_pos))))
d_cast_pos$cruise_key <- d_bind$cruise_key[match(d_cast_pos$gid, cast_gid)]
d_cast_pos$cast_id    <- d_bind$cast_id[match(d_cast_pos$gid, cast_gid)]
d_cast_pos <- d_cast_pos |>
  mutate(
    cast_base = str_remove(cast_id, "[dDuU]$"),
    km_cast = {
      r <- pi / 180
      2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(sin((lat_lnst - lat_med) * r / 2)^2 +
        cos(lat_med * r) * cos(lat_lnst * r) * sin((lon_lnst - lon_med) * r / 2)^2))
    }) |>
  left_join(CTD_OFF_STATION_KEEP |> select(cruise_key, cast_base, max_km),
            by = c("cruise_key", "cast_base")) |>
  mutate(
    is_off_station_kept = !is.na(km_cast) & km_cast > CTD_TRUNC_KM &
      !is.na(max_km) & km_cast <= max_km,
    is_on_station = !is.na(km_cast) & (km_cast <= CTD_TRUNC_KM | is_off_station_kept))

# an off-station allowance that no longer applies is a stale key, not a no-op
off_unused <- anti_join(CTD_OFF_STATION_KEEP,
                        d_cast_pos |> filter(is_off_station_kept), by = c("cruise_key", "cast_base"))
if (nrow(off_unused) > 0)
  stop(glue("CTD_OFF_STATION_KEEP matches no off-station cast: ",
            "{paste(off_unused$cruise_key, off_unused$cast_base, collapse = '; ')}"))
d_cast_pos |>
  filter(is_off_station_kept) |>
  transmute(cruise_key, cast_id, lon_med, lat_med, km_from_station = round(km_cast, 2), n_scans) |>
  dt(caption = "Casts kept off their nominal station (CTD_OFF_STATION_KEEP)",
     fname = "ctd_casts_off_station_kept")

d_bind$is_cast_on_station <- d_cast_pos$is_on_station[cast_gid]
i_glitch <- which(
  d_bind$is_cast_on_station &
    pmax(abs(d_bind$longitude - d_cast_pos$lon_med[cast_gid]),
         abs(d_bind$latitude  - d_cast_pos$lat_med[cast_gid])) > CTD_GLITCH_DEG)
if (length(i_glitch) > 0) {
  tibble(cruise_key = d_bind$cruise_key[i_glitch], cast_id = d_bind$cast_id[i_glitch],
         depth = d_bind$depth[i_glitch]) |>
    group_by(cruise_key) |>
    summarize(n_casts = n_distinct(cast_id), n_scans = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
    dt(caption = glue(
      "GPS glitches: scans more than {CTD_GLITCH_DEG} deg from their on-station cast's ",
      "median position, kept with the cast's median position"),
      fname = "ctd_scans_gps_glitch")
  say(glue("GPS-glitch scans given their cast's median position: ",
           "{format(length(i_glitch), big.mark = ',')} on ",
           "{n_distinct(cast_gid[i_glitch])} cast(s)"))
  d_bind$longitude[i_glitch] <- d_cast_pos$lon_med[cast_gid[i_glitch]]
  d_bind$latitude[i_glitch]  <- d_cast_pos$lat_med[cast_gid[i_glitch]]
}
write_rds(d_cast_pos, glue("{dir_tmp}/d_cast_position.rds"))
rm(cast_gid, i_glitch)

d_bind |>
  filter(is_lon_pseudoNA | is_lat_pseudoNA) |>
  group_by(cruise_key) |>
  summarize(
    n_lon_pseudoNA = sum(is_lon_pseudoNA),
    n_lat_pseudoNA = sum(is_lat_pseudoNA)
  ) |>
  dt(
    caption = glue(
      "Cruises with pseudo-NAs ({paste(pseudoNA_values, collapse = ',')}) ",
      "set to NA, then filled from line/station coordinates."
    ),
    fname = "ctd_cruises_pseudoNA_lonlat"
  ) |>
  formatCurrency(
    c("n_lon_pseudoNA", "n_lat_pseudoNA"),
    currency = "",
    digits = 0,
    mark = ","
  )
```

## Distance Filtering

```{r}
#| label: pts_distance_from_lnst

max_dist_dec_lnst_km <- 10

# THIS USED TO MATERIALIZE EVERY SCAN AS AN sf OBJECT WITH TWO GEOMETRY COLUMNS.
# With 45 more cruises that stopped fitting: `pts` reached the machine's 24 GB
# ceiling and `filter_pts` died with "vector memory limit of 24.0 Gb reached"
# after the distance step alone had run for 74 minutes. Both symptoms came from
# doing point work at the wrong grain, so fix the grain rather than the limit —
# raising mem.maxVSize on a 24 GB machine only buys swapping, and DuckDB is
# already holding half of RAM.
#
# Three changes, none of which alters a single output value:
#
#  1. The nominal line/station coordinate takes ~200 distinct values in the whole
#     dataset — one per CalCOFI grid station — but `purrr::map2(st_point)` built
#     one sfg per SCAN, i.e. ~30M R-level closure calls to produce ~200 distinct
#     points. Build the lookup once and join it on.
#  2. Run per cruise. Every operation here is row-wise (distance by_element) or a
#     point-in-polygon against a static grid, so there is no cross-cruise
#     dependency and batching is exactly equivalent — it just bounds peak memory
#     to one cruise instead of the whole archive.
#  3. Return PLAIN TIBBLES. Nothing downstream wants geometry: `d_filt` already
#     did `st_drop_geometry() |> select(-geom_lnst)`, and the two map previews
#     below rebuild it from lon/lat on a ~100-point sample.

grid_ref <- calcofi4r::cc_grid |>
  rename(any_of(c(site_key = "sta_key"))) |>
  select(grid_site = site_key)

# ~200 rows: the distinct nominal station coordinates, as points, built once
lnst_ref <- d_bind |>
  distinct(lon_lnst, lat_lnst) |>
  filter(!is.na(lon_lnst), !is.na(lat_lnst)) |>
  mutate(
    geom_lnst = purrr::map2(lon_lnst, lat_lnst, \(x, y) st_point(c(x, y))) |>
      st_sfc(crs = 4326))

say(glue("Distance filter: {nrow(lnst_ref)} distinct station coordinates ",
         "across {format(nrow(d_bind), big.mark = ',')} scans"))

# compute the three derived columns for one cruise, and only those columns — the
# batch results are bound and joined back, so d_bind is never duplicated
dist_one_cruise <- function(d) {
  s <- d |>
    select(.row_id, longitude, latitude, lon_lnst, lat_lnst) |>
    left_join(lnst_ref, by = c("lon_lnst", "lat_lnst")) |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), remove = FALSE, crs = 4326)

  # a scan with no nominal coordinate gets NA distance, exactly as st_distance
  # against an empty geometry did before
  s$dist_dec_lnst_km <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(s))
  has <- !st_is_empty(s$geom_lnst) & !is.na(s$lon_lnst)
  if (any(has))
    s$dist_dec_lnst_km[has] <- st_distance(
      st_geometry(s)[has], s$geom_lnst[has], by_element = TRUE) |>
      units::set_units(km) |>
      units::drop_units()

  s$is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max <- s$dist_dec_lnst_km <= max_dist_dec_lnst_km
  s$geom_lnst <- NULL
  st_agr(s) <- "constant"

  s |>
    st_join(grid_ref, join = st_intersects) |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    select(.row_id, dist_dec_lnst_km, is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max, grid_site)
}

d_bind <- d_bind |> mutate(.row_id = row_number())

# The batch results are three columns plus an id — assign them into d_bind by
# column rather than joining. A `right_join` back would allocate a second copy of
# the whole ~30M-row frame, which on a 24 GB machine is the very thing that
# killed the previous run.
# only the columns dist_one_cruise() reads: group_split() COPIES what it splits, and
# splitting the whole ~110-column frame doubled R's peak (2026-09-23: 24 GB limit)
d_dist <- d_bind |>
  select(.row_id, cruise_key, longitude, latitude, lon_lnst, lat_lnst) |>
  group_split(cruise_key) |>
  purrr::map(dist_one_cruise) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  arrange(.row_id)

stopifnot(
  "distance batches must cover every scan exactly once, in order" =
    identical(d_dist$.row_id, d_bind$.row_id))

d_bind$dist_dec_lnst_km            <- d_dist$dist_dec_lnst_km
d_bind$is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max <- d_dist$is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max
d_bind$grid_site                   <- d_dist$grid_site
rm(d_dist)

pts <- d_bind |> select(-.row_id)
```

### View sample cruise with excess distance points

```{r}
#| label: view_badcr

badcr_id <- "1507OC"

# `pts` is a plain tibble now (see pts_distance_from_lnst) — geometry is rebuilt
# here, on the sampled subset this map actually draws, rather than being carried
# on all ~30M scans just so two previews can use it
as_pts_sf <- function(d) st_as_sf(
  d, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), remove = FALSE, crs = 4326)

# the extent from the lon/lat COLUMNS. st_bbox() would have to build geometry for
# every row first, which is the allocation this chunk exists to avoid — and the
# bounding box of a point set is just four numbers.
pts_bbox <- function(d) st_bbox(
  c(xmin = min(d$longitude, na.rm = TRUE), ymin = min(d$latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    xmax = max(d$longitude, na.rm = TRUE), ymax = max(d$latitude, na.rm = TRUE)),
  crs = st_crs(4326))

pts_badcr <- pts |>
  filter(cruise_key == badcr_id)

bb_badcr <- pts_badcr |> pts_bbox() |> st_as_sfc()

mapView(bb_badcr) +
  mapView(
    pts_badcr |>
      filter(is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max) |>
      slice_sample(n = 1000) |>
      bind_rows(
        pts_badcr |>
          filter(!is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max)
      ) |>
      as_pts_sf() |>
      select(
        cruise_key,
        datetime_start_utc,
        longitude,
        latitude,
        sta_id,
        line,
        sta,
        dist_dec_lnst_km,
        is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max
      ),
    layer.name = glue(
      "Cruise {badcr_id}<br>distance (km)<br>lon/lat to line/station"
    ),
    zcol = "dist_dec_lnst_km",
    cex = 5,
    alpha = 0.5
  )
```

### Filter points

```{r}
#| label: filter_pts

# a scan stays when its CAST is on station ([fill_lonlat]: median position, glitches
# repositioned) or, for a cast whose median fails, when the scan itself is within the
# cutoff (the pre-#131 rule, so a cast with a GPS feed corrupt on most scans keeps what
# it kept). is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max is folded into that verdict here.
pts$is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max <- pts$is_cast_on_station | pts$is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max

d_pts_cruise_filt_smry <- pts |>
  group_by(cruise_key) |>
  filter(any(!is_dist_dec_lnst_within_max)) |>
  summarize(
    n_all = n(),
```
